544088|2026-03.headline: Medi Assist FY26: total income up 23.6% to INR923.2 crore, operating EBITDA margin 19.3%, company turned debt-free in Jan 2026.
544088|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong top-line growth with total income of INR923.2 crore (up 23.6% YoY) and operating income of INR904.8 crore (up 25.1%). Operating EBITDA reached INR174.6 crore at a 19.3% margin, with quarterly margin expanding from 17.1% in Q2 to 18.6% in Q3 and 19.9% in Q4. Reported PAT was INR89.3 crore, while adjusted PAT was INR68.8 crore after exceptional items. The group became debt-free in January 2026, and Paramount TPA operations were transferred into Medi Assist TPA effective 1 February 2026.

segments.name: Group
segments.commentary: Revenue INR629.1 crore, about 69.5% of total, up 25.3% YoY. Group premium under administration above INR23,000 crore (up 25.6%), with retention of 93.2%, below the historical 94%+.

segments.name: Retail (TPA model)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR95.5 crore, about 10.6% of total, up 10.9% YoY. TPA-model retail premium INR2,818 crore (up 4.2%); market share 5%, slightly lower YoY. Premiums on MAtrix for private insurers exceed INR18,000 crore (about 32% of industry retail premium).

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Revenue INR113.6 crore, about 12.6% of total, up 42.6% YoY. Work spans 13 states and 3 union territories.

segments.name: International Benefits Administration
segments.commentary: Revenue INR41.1 crore, about 4.5% of total, up 11.9% YoY. Management said there is little or no exposure to the Middle East; a group-segment slowdown was seen from IT-ITES headcount cuts.

segments.name: Technology SaaS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21.7 crore, about 2.5% of total, up 91.9% YoY. Current revenue comes only from the core SaaS claims platform (MAtrix), with no AI or outcome-based features yet billed.

guidance_outlook: Paramount TPA integration: over 50% of Paramount Health Services' claims volume migrated to MAtrix; full migration to primary processing engine expected before Q2 FY27. Management tracks to synergies within 1-2 quarters from now, against a 4-5 quarter norm.
Technology and international revenue growth expected to continue at similar rates to FY26 or better, per management.
Core business expected to match or beat industry growth; management cited 8-10% blended same-store group growth currently.
Management gave a directional aspiration (explicitly not guidance) that technology margins could be 1.5-2x the traditional TPA business as non-headcount yield is captured.
Exceptional items (including insurance claims and disallowed claims) remain open and will be carried each quarter until resolved.
capex_capacity: Nearly one million claims processed per month on AI-powered platforms, per management.
MAven Guard fraud detection prevented over INR540 crore of frauds in FY26; network discounts delivered over INR1,300 crore last year.
Raksha Prime enabled over 322,000 patients to walk out before bills were generated, across 6,000 hospitals in FY26.
Nearly one-third of headcount is contractually obligated to public-health schemes, serving 27 crore members.
AI capabilities can now be deployed on top of legacy or third-party claims platforms, not only on MAtrix.
demand_pricing: Total premium under management INR25,923 crore as of 31 March 2026, up 22.8%; market share of group plus retail in total health premium 20.7%, up 115 bps.
Group market share up 340 bps to 33.7%; group premium grew 25.6% including Paramount.
Group yields are compressing partly because of low-ticket-size benefit add-ons that are not fully priced; management says effort-to-remuneration metrics remain healthy.
Group same-store growth has slowed from about 25% post-COVID to an estimated 8-10% blended; over INR2,000 crore of new group premium added organically in FY26.
IT-ITES headcount reductions are the main drag on group lives; other sectors such as oil and gas and chemicals are growing.
Management views outcome-based pricing as the eventual direction for AI-led services; no fixed-price AI contracts exist today.
Management estimated the Indian health premium administered by TPAs at roughly 50% of the market, with the other 50% in areas like personal accident outside TPA scope.

qa_highlights.question: How can the company build dominance in retail given its strength in group?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described retail as a hybrid model: TPA-led for high-frequency outpatient products and technology plug-ins for insurers' own front ends, with the premium under MAtrix reported separately.

qa_highlights.question: How can investors track earnings on the technology business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose a take rate. It offered a directional aspiration of 1.5-2x traditional TPA margins, stating this was not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is group retention (93.2%) below last year and what about PSU allocations?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention dipped due to deliberate quality-of-revenue decisions and operational transition; management expects a return to slightly higher retention. PSU allocations are driven by insurer cycles and are outside the company's control.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Bima Sugam on the business over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect disruption, arguing claims adjudication, network, and fraud control remain needed; it cited integration with NHCX and work in 13 states and 3 UTs contributing over INR113 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How far can AI automate claims, and could take rates fall from around 3.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most claims processing is rule-driven and targets 70-80% automation; it declined to forecast yield changes, attributing yield compression to lower-ticket benefit products.

qa_highlights.question: Paramount integration timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said integration is 3 quarters in with Q4 margins up about 130 bps QoQ, and expects synergies within 1-2 more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to the Middle East conflict and the exceptional item recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: No material Middle East exposure; the international slowdown was limited to group, with some operational challenges on seafarer cover. Exceptional items remain open and are disclosed in the notes.

risks_watch: Group same-store growth slowing (about 8-10% blended) with IT-ITES headcount cuts; watch lives growth in non-IT sectors.
Group retention at 93.2%, below the historical 94%+; watch for recovery in Q1 FY27.
Yield compression from low-ticket benefit products; management did not give a forward view on take rate.
Paramount migration to MAtrix before Q2 FY27 and synergy delivery in 1-2 quarters.
Regulatory and policy risk from Bima Sugam and the National Health Claims Exchange; management sees no near-term disruption.
Retail TPA-model premium growth of only 4.2% and market share slipping to 5%.
Technology revenue remains about 2.5% of total; watch disclosed growth of AI modules and first outcome-based contracts.
Open exceptional items and insurance claims on disallowed items continue into subsequent quarters.
544088|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins, and technology, with clear statements on Paramount integration timing. Evasive or non-committal on yield trajectory, take rate, and specific guidance, which management repeatedly labelled as not guidance. Cautious on group growth given IT-ITES headcount cuts.
key_quotes: Becoming debt-free and net cash positive strengthens our ability to invest in the future, while our AI-powered platforms are now operating at unprecedented scale, processing nearly 1 million claims every month with industry-leading automation and fraud detection.
We're 3 quarters down. And I think our quarterly margins in Q4 also went up by another 130 bps compared to Q3.
Much as we would like to say AI will automate a claim. What we need AI for right now urgently in the country is to make sure inputs are good enough for the rule engines.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 up ~130 bps QoQ per management

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (excl. exceptional items, net of tax)

rows.why: Quarterly operating EBITDA margin rose from 17.1% in Q2 to 18.6% in Q3 and 19.9% in Q4, and management expects Paramount synergies within 1-2 quarters, though group yields are compressing from low-ticket add-ons.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects technology and international revenue growth at similar-to-FY26 rates or better (FY26 group revenue +25.3%, technology +91.9%), and core business to match or beat industry growth at 8-10% blended same-store, with group market share up 340 bps to 33.7%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Paramount synergies are expected within 1-2 quarters against a 4-5 quarter norm, and Q4 margin rose about 130 bps QoQ to 19.9%, which could lift the outlook if delivered.

rows.why: Group same-store growth slowed from about 25% post-COVID to an estimated 8-10% blended, retention fell to 93.2% (below the historical 94%+), and IT-ITES headcount cuts are a drag on group lives, so the core growth outlook could be missed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Technology revenue is only INR21.7 crore (2.5% of total) with no AI or outcome-based features billed yet, and management says AI can now be deployed on legacy platforms, so first billed AI modules could appear but no date was given.

rows.label: Paramount TPA migration to MAtrix and synergy delivery
rows.when: full migration before Q2 FY27; synergies within 1-2 quarters
rows.why: Over 50% of Paramount's claims volume has already moved to MAtrix, and management tracks to synergies in 1-2 quarters against a 4-5 quarter norm, after Q4 margin rose about 130 bps QoQ.

rows.label: Group retention recovery to 94%+
rows.why: Retention fell to 93.2% from the historical 94%+ due to deliberate quality-of-revenue decisions; management expects a return to slightly higher retention, but PSU allocations sit outside its control.

544088|2026-06.headline: Medi Assist Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 20.3% and retention down to 90.2%.
544088|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore and group revenue grew 25.5%, while operating EBITDA rose 14.3% to INR48 crore at a 20.3% margin. Reported PAT was INR27.6 crore, or INR24.5 crore excluding a one-time INR3.1 crore derivative gain. Retention fell to 90.2% in the quarter, which management attributed to Paramount book transition, portfolio rationalisation and a high base. Management also announced the separation of Chairman and CEO roles, with Dr. Chhatwal moving to Non-Executive Chairman subject to AGM approval on 8 September.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating revenue (revenue from contracts, excl. other income)

financial_highlights.change: Includes one-time INR3.1 crore derivative gain; normative PAT INR24.5 crore

segments.name: Group TPA
segments.commentary: Revenue INR166 crore, up 25.5% YoY, with group market share at 37.6%. Same-store growth averaged about 7-8%, slower in large IT companies and faster elsewhere.

segments.name: Retail TPA
segments.commentary: Retail TPA-model revenue INR23.4 crore, up 13.1% YoY. Management says platform-administered retail premiums reached over INR4,254 crore, about 29% market share, versus INR521 crore TPA-model premiums.

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28.5 crore, up 35.3% YoY, now across 16 states; management called it margin accretive and said it serves over 31 crore members across 12 states and 4 UTs under TPA model.

segments.name: International (Mayfair)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR10.1 crore, down 5.2% YoY, hit by softness in student, leisure and marine volumes. Ownership raised to 91.75%; first technology contract went live in Thailand from 1 July 2026.

segments.name: Technology SaaS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7.8 crore, up 55.5% YoY, 3.3% of consolidated revenue. Fraud savings from MAven Guard exceeded INR183 crore in Q1; 7 insurers contracted across MAven, MAtrix and Magnum stacks.

guidance_outlook: Complete the Paramount integration: over 95% of group claims and over 80% of retail claims were on MAtrix at Q1 end, with the balance targeted for Q2 FY27.
Management expects Paramount-related retention drag to normalise through FY27 and EBITDA margin to return towards the pre-integration 22-23% level by the end of FY27.
Management says group and retail will grow at par with or faster than the market; government growth is opportunistic.
Management expects technology and international to become meaningful contributors to growth and EBITDA margin over time, funded from operating cash flows.
capex_capacity: Company spent about INR24.5 crore on its AI stack over the last six quarters under a Board-approved roadmap, funded from operating cash flows.
MAtrix implementation at Star crossed 90%.
Platform processed over 186,000 pre-authorisations within 5 minutes in Q1; Raksha Prime delivered zero-wait discharge for over 87,000 members across 6,000 hospitals.
Company remains debt-free.
demand_pricing: Retention at 90.2% in Q1, below the historical 93-94%, due to onboarding challenges with a large acquired book, portfolio rationalisation and a higher base.
Management says its PSU group premium growth of 28.9% compares with industry PSU group premiums down about 1.5%, while overall group health industry growth was about 14%.
DSO improved 4.5 percentage points versus the prior-year trend for the quarter, on a higher receivables base.
Revenue per average headcount on non-government contracts was INR13.2 lakh annualised.
Management said international Q1 is not representative, citing softness in student, leisure and marine volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How should retail business trajectory be interpreted, given the traditional TPA model looks plateaued while technology grows fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TPA-model retail line is reported narrowly, so it should be viewed alongside platform and technology revenue, which together indicate market-share gains. Platform-administered retail premiums are over INR4,254 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a margin recovery to 23%, and is FY27 likely to be a record profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the immediate priority is finishing Paramount integration and returning to the 22-23% margin band towards the end of FY27. It did not give a FY27 profit target and does not break out margins by line of business.

qa_highlights.question: Does government business strain working capital, and should revenue from it be capped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government collections are the safest as they come from state and central governments, and it is margin accretive. Consolidated DSOs include government and are improving.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic growth of the legacy group TPA book, and what is the outcome-based contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retention is about 90%, same-store growth is about 7-8%, and new business seasonality distorts quarterly figures. It declined to give the outcome-based contract details beyond saying it is tied to fraud, waste and abuse outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of PSU TPA in-housing (HITPA) shifting premiums away from Medi Assist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not comment on specific TPAs, that the policyholder-choice regulation supports it, and that its share of wallet has improved in both PSU and private group.

qa_highlights.question: What is NPS Swasthya and what is the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is the health benefit administrator and technology platform connecting NPS members, CRAs, pension funds, insurers and networks, and that it is at an early stage with potential platform and incremental TPA revenue.

risks_watch: Group retention at 90.2% versus the historical 93-94%; management did not disclose a breakdown of the retention figure.
Paramount integration completion and the target to move the remaining claims to the MAtrix stack in Q2 FY27.
PSU in-housing (HITPA) trend could shift group premiums away from the company.
International revenue fell 5.2% YoY; student, leisure and marine volumes are soft.
Management did not provide a separate depreciation breakdown; this was deferred offline.

So it's a true reflection of the generic capabilities of the pl atforms we have built and is an indication of the work that we can do in markets outside India.
It's a little hard for us to break that out today.
Yes, that is true. I mean our share of wallet has improved. In fact, in both the segments, both in PSU and private, our share of wallet has improved, yes.

544095|2026-03.headline: EPACK Q4 FY26 revenue fell about 8% YoY to Rs 591 crore and EBITDA margin compressed to 4.37%, with a Rs 32.42 crore PLI reversal weighing on the quarter.
544095|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 591 crore, down about 8% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 25.8 crore (down about 64% YoY) and a 4.37% margin versus 11.21%. Net profit was Rs 2.4 lakh after a Rs 32.42 crore reversal of PLI income accrued in the first nine months and Rs 21.78 crore of RIPS 2024 incentive recognised in the quarter. For FY26, revenue was Rs 1,894 crore (down 12.7%), EBITDA Rs 113.9 crore (down 27.7%), margin 6.01%, and net profit Rs 3.3 crore. Management said early FY27 trends look better, with industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 and a strong order book.

financial_highlights.change: of which Rs 4.96 crore relates to FY26 and Rs 16.82 crore to earlier periods
accrued in the nine months to Dec 31, 2025

segments.name: RAC (room air conditioners)
segments.commentary: Q4 RAC revenue fell about 25% YoY, versus about 33% decline in the first three quarters. FY26 RAC utilisation fell to roughly 20-odd% (about 40% by the management's alternative framing) from 45-50% previously; peak-season utilisation fell to about 75% from about 90%.

segments.name: SDA and LDA (small and large domestic appliances)
segments.commentary: Grew about 53% YoY in the quarter, supported by order inflows across existing and new products; air fryers cited as encouraging.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Grew about 50% YoY in the quarter on localisation requirements and deeper customer integration; heat exchangers, injection-moulded parts, PCBs and copper components flagged as priorities.

segments.name: Hisense JV (EPACK Manufacturing Technologies, Sri City)
segments.commentary: Became operational around March 30, 2026 for Hisense-design AC production; washing machine production expected to start around mid-Q2 FY27 after trials.

segments.name: Epavo JV (motors, Bhiwadi)
segments.commentary: New greenfield facility operational since end-Q3 FY26, mass production from January 2026, roughly 3 million motors per annum installed capacity; the JV's losses roughly doubled in FY26 per an analyst, with about Rs 100 crore invested.

guidance_outlook: Industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 FY27; management said EPACK should outgrow the industry in FY27 but declined to quantify.
Management reiterated a target of about Rs 5,000 crore revenue in the next two to three years.
Asset turn was about 2.6 in FY26 versus 3.2 in FY25; management targets about 4 in the medium to long term.

Normalised gross margin cited at 13-14% and normalised EBITDA around 7%, with improvement expected as utilisation rises; management said historical EBITDA-level stability was 7.5-8.25% over four years.

FY27 is the final year of PLI incentive; the company is eligible for about Rs 60 crore but will not recognise it until revenue thresholds are confirmed. Management said incentives should be treated as above the core margin.
Remaining capex of Rs 170-200 crore planned over the next 9-12 months against a Rs 470 crore budget (Rs 300 crore already capitalised), mainly Bhiwadi and Sri City.
capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 capex about Rs 79 crore, mainly washing machine capacity and component manufacturing; about Rs 300 crore capitalised in the last four quarters against a Rs 470 crore 18-24 month budget.
Remaining capex of Rs 170-200 crore planned over the next 9-12 months, mainly for Bhiwadi and Sri City capacity and new product categories.

Hisense facility at Sri City started production in the last week of March 2026, with AC production scaling for about two months; front-load washing machines under trial with production expected around mid-Q2 FY27.
Epavo Bhiwadi greenfield motor facility capacity about 3 million motors per annum; mass production from January 2026.
Greenfield facility at Bhiwadi expected to contribute meaningfully over coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Management said the post-stabilisation trend from mid-April is strong, with sell-in picking up and trade inventory normalised; industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 FY27.
Price increases of 15-20% (model-dependent) were passed on by end-March 2026 across commodity, BEE re-rating and geopolitical triggers, with a further increase in April and May.
Management said the industry channel plus brand inventory as of May opening was about 4-4.5 million units, slightly below expected norms.
Customer additions: 17 new customers in FY26 (5 added in Q4) for a total active base of 72; 5 are large multinational cooling customers and the rest are top-10 small domestic appliance players.
Old BEE-rated inventory is not held by EPACK (last shipments by December 31, 2025); management sees no liability on that front.
Compressor sourcing about 60% domestic and 40% imported; government relaxation allows about 30% imports following a May 8 circular.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the PLI benefit reversed and what were the eligibility conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the criteria were investment in the prior year and 5x incremental revenue growth for applicable components; capex was met but incremental revenue shortfall led to reversal of Rs 32.42 crore, pending auditor review and government clarification. The total FY26 eligibility was about Rs 56.5 crore, with only about Rs 32 crore accrued before Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off net effect on profit (around Rs 11-12 crore per an analyst)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is larger: the Rs 32.42 crore reversal plus Rs 24 crore of unrecognised Q4 PLI, leaving a difference of about Rs 35-36 crore versus the full eligibility, after Rs 21 crore of RIPS was booked.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the sharp rise in inventory and payables days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the working-capital build to summer-season inventory, imported compressors stocked ahead of a BIS expiry in mid-April, and payables rising in step; inventory was about Rs 800-837 crore at end-March and management expects normalisation by quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue double in two to three years and will EPACK outgrow the industry in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the Rs 5,000 crore ambition in two to three years and said EPACK should outgrow the roughly 15% industry growth, but gave no numeric guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken and will margins compress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cumulative price increases of 15-20% were taken by end-March, with a further rise in April and May; some lag is expected in Q1, with a Y-o-Y margin squeeze but some sequential improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RAC utilisation level in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annualised utilisation fell to roughly 20-40% (figures given inconsistently) from 45-50% historically; peak-season utilisation fell to about 75% from about 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Hisense JV exposed to China-related policy risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPACK funded the Sri City facility itself under a tech-transfer arrangement, sees no policy impact, and expects Hisense to expand into washing machines and other products in Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the auditor qualification about?
qa_highlights.answer: The qualification relates to a Rs 19.61 crore receivable from customer Gangnam, which is sub judice; management said it believes the amount is recoverable and has filed legal complaints.

risks_watch: Quality of earnings: Q4 net profit of Rs 2.4 lakh was after a Rs 32.42 crore PLI reversal and Rs 21.78 crore RIPS income; the PLI reversal could be reinstated, but management said it will wait at least another quarter for clarity.
Working capital: inventory of about Rs 800-837 crore and trade payable days rising to about 130-140 from about 90-100 need to normalise; watch the next quarter's inventory and payables.
Margin pass-through lag from commodity and forex moves, which management said is unpredictable; Q1 FY27 margins still expected below prior-year levels YoY.
Receivable of Rs 19.61 crore from Gangnam under legal dispute and flagged by auditors as a qualification.

Asset turn fell to about 2.6 from 3.2; debt about Rs 700 crore including a Rs 200 crore term loan.

544095|2026-06.headline: EPACK Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR886 crore (+34% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 6.21% from 8.24% as PLI income dropped to nil.
544095|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose about 34% YoY to INR886 crore, the company's highest quarterly revenue, with RAC up about 44% (roughly 30% volume, 14% value). EBITDA was INR55 crore, up about 0.7% YoY, with margin at 6.21% versus 8.24%; management said the prior-year figure included INR13.31 crore of PLI income, and the like-for-like underlying margin was about 6.4% in Q1 FY26. Net profit was INR11.8 crore, and management cited a forex loss of about INR6-7 crore and higher wage costs as pressures. Management said FY27 is the last year of PLI benefit and is rolling back PLI discounts shared with brand customers, aiming to fully reverse them by year-end.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.24% in Q1 FY26; ~6.4% underlying ex-PLI in Q1 FY26
vs INR13.31 crore in Q1 FY26
from ~INR80 crore last year; Q1 growth ~68% YoY

segments.commentary: Revenue about INR660 crore of the INR886 crore total; growth ~44% with ~30% from volume. Hisense JV delivered ~35,000 ACs in Q1 (~60,000 in Jan-Jun season) for ~INR65 crore Q1 revenue (~INR120 crore for the season).

segments.name: SDA + LDA (small and large domestic appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR130 crore vs ~INR80 crore last year per management; Q1 growth ~68% YoY. Gross margin reportedly 1.5-2 percentage points above AC (stated as 'basis points', likely a units slip). Washing machines: top-load fully automatic in production for 3 national/multinational brands; front-load pilot underway, mass production targeted by end-Sept/October 2026.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 23% (question-referenced figure, not confirmed by management); components are largely AC-linked (controllers, cross-flow fans, copper tubing) and seasonal. Management said growth will continue and non-AC components are being explored.

guidance_outlook: Industry AC growth expected ~20% in FY27; management expects EPACK to outgrow the industry. No formal numerical guidance given on revenue.
Target utilisation of all three plants (Dehradun, Bhiwadi, Sri City) at 55-60% for FY27 average; management said more than 60% on average.
Q2 and Q3 have historically been loss-making; management targets stopping the 'bleeding' in these quarters within 4-6 quarters, but declined to say whether Q2 FY27 will be PAT positive.
PLI discount rollback: aim to reverse fully by end-FY27; PLI ends with FY27, and normalised EBITDA expected from FY28. Prior commentary: ~6.5% EBITDA ex-PLI for recent quarters.

Capex: total budget ~INR450-470 crore; ~INR330-350 crore booked; INR60-70 crore additional capex expected in the remaining nine months; depreciation not expected to rise significantly over next three quarters.
Hisense: cumulative expected revenue of ~INR8,000 crore over five years; management said on track for calendar 2026 and front-load washing machine production by end-October.
Andhra Pradesh MoU: INR1,085 crore investment over five years, ~35 acres allotted; state investment subsidy about 50% of capex over 10 years.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR10 crore; ~INR60 crore in CWIP expected to capitalise over the next two quarters.
Sri City plant utilisation close to 50% in Q1 FY27 vs under 25% previously reported; Dehradun and Bhiwadi utilisation above 85-90% in Q1.
FY26 utilisation: Dehradun and Bhiwadi ~55%, Sri City below 25%.
Washing machine and LDA capacity ramp flagged as fastest-growing; front-load washing machine pilot to mass production around end-Oct 2026.

Compressors: management said domestic compressor capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) is sufficient; imports allowed until end of calendar 2026. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.
demand_pricing: RAC: channel inventory considered largely liquidated after old-BEE-rated stock sell-through allowed until end-June 2026; management estimates industry inventory at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level.

Pricing: contracts with large customers reset prices quarterly; most commodity pass-through completed with a time lag, and management said little price increase remains to be passed on. Forex was the main margin headwind.

Customer base: 72 customers and 19 product categories at FY26 close; ~73 customers and 19 product lines now, targeting ~75 customers and 20 product lines by end-FY27. Three new categories added in Q1, four more in pipeline.
Commodities: no forward hedging; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.
Inventory: in-house inventory mix roughly 70-75% AC and 25-30% non-AC; working capital days ~50-60, with inventory elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions.

qa_highlights.question: Top 2-3 execution priorities and biggest risks (demand, regulation, competition)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AC tailwinds continuing and faster growth in SDA/LDA (washing machines) and components, with more customers added across categories. No specific risk list was given beyond the outlook commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the ~44% RAC growth between volume and value, and whether the volume growth is anchor-customer driven?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% volume and about 14% value (AOP increases and commodity pass-through). Management confirmed the volume growth is largely from the anchor customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost escalation is still to be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts reset prices quarterly and the prior quarter's increase was already passed on; little remains. The main margin hit was forex, which produced a loss of about INR6-7 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory levels and working capital trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry inventory estimated at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level. Working capital days are about 50-60, with in-house inventory still slightly elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions; the company aims to normalise it.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor supply risk as BIS/QCO relief expires around March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed until end of calendar 2026, with domestic capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) judged sufficient. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for depreciation, finance cost and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation not expected to rise significantly over the next three quarters. Finance cost rose about INR3-4 crore QoQ on ~40% growth, with scope to reduce via inventory normalisation. Total capex budget ~INR450-470 crore, with ~INR330-350 crore booked and INR60-70 crore more over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue and EBITDA margin outlook; PLI impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal revenue guidance; industry AC growth ~20% expected and EPACK to outgrow it. Ex-PLI EBITDA ~6.5% in recent quarters; PLI worth roughly 1-2% of margin, shared ~50:50 with customers. Management is rolling back PLI discounts with the aim of full reversal by year-end, with normalised EBITDA from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Sri City utilisation, operating leverage and FY27 utilisation target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri City reached close to 50% in Q1 FY27 (from under 25%), while Dehradun and Bhiwadi ran above 85%. Management targets 55-60% average across the three plants for FY27, and said it is above 60% on average.

qa_highlights.question: Hisense progress and washing machine timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60,000 ACs delivered Jan-Jun season for ~INR120 crore revenue; Q1 alone ~35,000 units for ~INR65 crore. Front-load washing machine pilot underway, mass production targeted by end-October. Management said the five-year ~INR8,000 crore plan is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity hedging policy, especially copper?
qa_highlights.answer: No forward booking in anticipation of orders; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 PAT positivity and structural seasonality fix, and the INR5,000 crore FY29 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 and Q3 have historically been loss-making; the company targets stopping this in 4-6 quarters and declined to guide on Q2 FY27 PAT. Top-load washing machines are in production for three national/multinational brands; management said it is largely on track for the FY29 INR5,000 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: Components revenue decline of about 23% and SDA/LDA margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the 23% figure but said components will keep growing; current components are AC-linked (controllers, cross-flow fans, copper tubing). SDA/LDA gross margin is about 1.5-2 percentage points above AC (the transcript says 'basis points'). Non-AC components are being explored.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the spike in other expenses (>50%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a forex loss of INR6-7 crore, plus higher wage costs from the 35%+ rise in sales and production value.

risks_watch: Forex losses (INR6-7 crore in Q1) and commodity costs such as copper, with no forward hedging, could keep compressing margins until PLI discounts are fully rolled back.
PLI roll-back to customers through FY27 and the end of PLI benefit: whether EBITDA moves toward ~6.5% ex-PLI and normalises from FY28.
Q2 and Q3 seasonality: whether front-load washing machine mass production (end-Sept/October 2026) and non-AC categories cut losses in these quarters; management declined to guide on Q2 FY27 PAT.
Sri City utilisation ramp (about 50% in Q1 vs under 25% in FY26) against the 55-60% FY27 target.
Working capital and finance cost: inventory still elevated from BIS/QCO revisions; finance cost up INR3-4 crore QoQ.
Compressor supply after import allowance ends in calendar 2026; BIS/QCO timing and copper QCO changes.
Capex execution of INR60-70 crore over nine months and capitalisation of ~INR60 crore CWIP; Hisense ramp versus the ~INR8,000 crore five-year cumulative plan.
key_quotes: So the entire strategy around SDA, LDA is first to neutralize the loss, and we are on track in terms of scaling up the washing machines and the other SDA businesses.

We are winning share, scaling the top line strongly and near-term profitability is being held back by the investment cycle and increase in input costs rather than by weakening in demand or competitiveness.
What impacted us most for the last quarter was especially the forex exchange rate.
So we are looking at overall utilization of all 3 plants put together at more than 60%.

544105|2026-03.headline: Harshdeep Hortico H2 FY26 revenue rose to INR 36.1 crore-range with EBITDA of INR 11.3 crore, but FY26 revenue of INR 69 crore missed the INR 85 crore internal expectation.
544105|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 H1 revenue of about INR 32.64 crore and H2 of about INR 36.1 crore, versus INR 24.9 crore and INR 31.51 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose to INR 8.4 crore in H1 and INR 11.3 crore in H2 (from INR 5.95 crore and INR 9.0 crore), and PAT to INR 5.7 crore and INR 6.82 crore. The CFO said full-year revenue of INR 69 crore fell short of the INR 85 crore expectation because of LPG gas cuts of about two months, raw material (PP) prices up 20-25% or more, and deferred luxury orders. Management said demand is holding flat year-on-year but not growing, and that margins are being defended by passing on only part of the cost increase.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B is about 75% and B2C about 25%, with pots purely B2B and garden furniture and fountains sold B2C. Current order book was about INR 1.5 crore of airport orders.

qa_highlights.question: Realistic FY27 revenue and three-year growth aspiration after the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a firm number, citing LPG cuts, labour shortage, raw material spikes and deferred projects. It said 25-30% annual growth is realistic if conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold around 30% after raw material inflation, and has price been raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices were raised about 20-25% on wholesale rates (not MRP), with the company holding back on full pass-through to avoid losing customers. Management said it will keep margins as high as possible.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising YoY, and what is the sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to inventory build for capacity growth and sudden orders (e.g., about INR 1 crore in two weeks for an event), plus credit to large customers and new stores. It gave no target number.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory (up 62%) and receivables (up 51%) growth due to pre-stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no pre-stocking; it held stock for only 15-20 working days during raw material shortages and expects the condition to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 EBITDA margin about 31% vs about 28% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, with H2 driven by festivals and landscaping projects and higher-margin roto moulded and decorative products, plus the new fountain launch.

qa_highlights.answer: Orders come through landscapers and subcontractors who tender on the company's behalf, as payment security is needed. Management said distributor and project margins are the same, with discounts of 45-50% based on order value, and the project margin is about 17%.

544111|2026-03.headline: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR 707 crore, with PAT of INR 66 crore; Q4 revenue up 4% to INR 184 crore.
544111|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR 184 crore (up 4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 53 crore (28.85% margin) and PAT of INR 12 crore (6.44% margin). Management blamed Q4 cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad on the Middle East war, saying occupancy there has recovered to over 90%. For FY26, revenue grew 12%, EBITDA was INR 218 crore (30.82% margin) and PAT was INR 66 crore (9.21% margin), with profitability hit by the Middle East war and higher depreciation and finance costs. Management reiterated the plan to double hotels to 85 and keys to 6,635 over four years, and said the EM Bypass Kolkata apartment sales are ahead of plan on cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Flurys outlet count below earlier guidance, and what is the achievable expansion plan?

qa_highlights.question: How is 100% occupancy at Park Calcutta calculated when the website shows rooms available?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata outlook and how is the EM Bypass sales progress?

qa_highlights.question: How will Flurys maintain quality with the central kitchen dropped?

qa_highlights.question: How will the company keep interest costs under control during the capex cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Atul Khosla said the interest rate is about 8.35% (MCLR) and will stay below that. Capex of about INR 1,500 crore over five years is mostly funded by internal accruals, with about INR 80 crore cash on hand; project interest will be capitalised as IDC.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the Vizag delay to 2030 and the status of Malabar House?

544111|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.

544119|2026-03.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
544119|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

financial_highlights.change: Described as healthy vs prior-year outflows

segments.name: PES (Personal computing / enterprise)
segments.commentary: About 58% of business; grew 37% YoY in FY26, aided by higher H2 PC demand and ASPs. Management expects ~20% average price increase in this category going forward.

segments.name: LIT (Lifestyle IT)
segments.commentary: About 42% of business; grew 24% YoY in FY26. Price increases described as routine only; management says LIT is growing about 2x the industry.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Grew 131% YoY from a small base; customers include large automotive, robotics and IoT manufacturers. Operations moved into a newly created subsidiary; management says meaningful P&L impact is a few years away.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a ~20% CAGR (sustained for 20 years) and expects to maintain this trajectory in FY27; regular-business growth aspiration of 15-20% YoY.
Management estimates PES unit market could degrow 5-10% in CY26 (IDC concurs), but with 20-25% price growth, PES revenue could still grow 10-15% on an as-is basis.
Consumer demand could soften in H2 FY27 on affordability; management is discussing 24- and 36-month interest-free EMI schemes with vendors.
Working capital days expected to stay in a similar range in FY27 (CFO).
Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% considered applicable to the industry absent mix change; margins described as intact despite price hikes.
Management said the super cycle could continue for another 1-2 years.
Project business (AI data centre) planned for FY27 subject to viability and ROI; funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores under consideration.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 55 city branch offices with three new branches added (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur, Maharashtra); 10,000-plus customers across 700-plus towns.
Working capital was increased on inventory to capture demand; management said inventory days cannot fall while regular business grows ~30%.
Project business: FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores of AI data centre project (Yotta, 512 servers, 4,000 GPUs); no substantial project business in FY26; FY27 plans subject to ROI.
Semiconductor business moved into a separate subsidiary to focus operations and accelerate partnerships and customer acquisition.
Management says it has post-IPO capacity to pick up data centre projects on a selective ROI basis without compromising regular growth.
demand_pricing: Price increases began mainly in H2 FY26; management estimates roughly half of H2 growth (46-47% H2-on-H2) came from pricing, i.e. ~20-22 percentage points.
Management says FY26 growth ex the one large AI project was 31%; FY26 growth without large deals was 15% reported.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 growth reported at 42% and 51% respectively (non-project business).

AI PCs are about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India; NVIDIA DGX Spark and Dell (server, storage, PCs, monitors) partnerships cited; Dell described as at low-single-digit share of revenue, expected to reach close to double digits next FY.
IDC: India traditional PC shipments 15.9 million units in CY2025 (+10.2%); IDC flags possible 5-10% dip in CY2026 shipments.
Enterprise refresh delayed by some large corporates during price hikes is reversing as buyers see 30-40% higher prices a year later.
Management said demand is not softening currently; affordability risk in consumer segment in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% is typical absent mix change; Q4 gross margin dip was due to additional provisioning for slow-moving inventory, not a structural decline.

risks_watch: Possible 5-10% unit decline in PC market in CY26 and H2 FY27 consumer softness from affordability as prices rise further.
Potential supply shortages in PES due to component (DRAM, NAND, GPU) pricing firmness.
Data centre project participation is capital-intensive with lower margins; scale of funnel conversion uncertain.
Inventory days (56) unlikely to fall while regular business grows ~30%; slow-moving inventory provision taken in Q4.
Semiconductor working capital cycle of 100-plus days; benefits to margin a few years away.
Dependence on Dell ramp-up (low-single-digit share now, expected near double-digit next FY).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: Funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration, but projects are subject to ROI and FY26 had no substantial project business (FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores Yotta project).

rows.label: PES price increases of ~20-25%
rows.why: Management expects ~20% average price increase in PES going forward; H2 FY26 pricing added about 20-22 points to H2 growth of 46-47%, and this supports PES revenue growth of 10-15% even as units fall 5-10%.

rows.why: CFO expects working capital days in a similar range (inventory 56, debtors 46, creditors 44, net 58 days), since inventory cannot fall while regular business grows about 30%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the PC super cycle, the 20% CAGR and the 1.5-1.75% PAT margin range, but evasive on Dell revenue numbers and deferred channel and margin questions offline; analysts probed price vs volume split, the Q4 gross margin dip and the AI data centre funnel.

544119|2026-06.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
544119|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

financial_highlights.change: up 55% YoY (CEO cited 50% on the opening remarks)

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5,102 crore and PAT Rs 105 crore; management stated all-time highs on topline, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE.

segments.name: Commercial vs consumer (B2B mix)
segments.commentary: Management estimates 30-35% consumer-centric and 60-65% commercial (SMB and enterprise). Consumer demand is slowing on affordability, with laptop prices reportedly about 2x year-on-year.

segments.name: Semiconductor / embedded
segments.commentary: Semiconductor revenue in Q1 grew about 70% versus the Q1 FY26 base (not 70% of full-year revenue, per clarification). Growth is described as near double-digit and sometimes higher.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (acquired)
segments.commentary: Majority stake (67% in year one) in a pan-India system integrator; FY26 revenue was about Rs 850 crore. Management expects integrated services and value-added solutions to be about 5% of revenue, with Q2 as the next update point.

Debt-to-equity ratio cited at around 0.5; management said large data centre projects could push it to at least 2x.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India demand strong relative to global peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price 30-35%, quantity 20-25%, new products and brands 5-10%, market share about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 should show a similar trend (about 60%), but the speed of price increases should roughly halve.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline: price or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix (higher PES share, lower margin than LIT) and to last year's hived-off subsidiary whose service cost sat in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply constraint risk in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is potential risk, but allocations so far are good given supplier relationships; the company tracks it weekly.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue large AI data centre deals aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised run-rate business with higher ROCE and working-capital needs; it still participates through smaller Rs 20-70 crore supplies and focuses on neo-clouds and smaller operators.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 look after the tailwinds fade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record and cited VDA and the Restar JV as longer-term growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor JV economics and Restar's investment amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Restar's investment depends on fair valuation at SPA signing, so it is not quantified; management targets over US$100 million JV revenue in three years and said the JV margin profile is higher than co-distribution.

Semiconductor JV: Restar's investment amount unquantified (depends on SPA valuation); JV numbers to be reported with Q2; VDA integration and contribution still undefined until Q2.

But yes, this is an orange alert for us. We track it on a weekly basis.

So, it is not that we are not there. It is only that we have not prioritized to do INR 500 crores or INR 1000 crores of deals

544120|2026-03.headline: Capital SFB Q4 FY26 PAT rose 17% YoY to ₹40 crores, with NIM up to 4.06% and FY27 ROA guided to 1.35%–1.4%.

Q4 PPOP rose 28% YoY to ₹62 crores and cost of deposits eased to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ, with NIM at 4.06% versus 4.01% in Q3. Asset quality was broadly stable: GNPA 2.54%, NNPA 1.24%, with Q4 credit cost of 0.26% driven by higher provisioning (PCR 51.89%) rather than losses. Management guided to FY27 advances growth of 22%+, ROA of 1.35%–1.4%, and credit cost of 0.15%–0.25%.

segments.commentary: Growth driver: +9% QoQ and +46% YoY in Q4. Management expects it to remain a growth leader in FY27.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: +5% QoQ and +19% YoY; yield 12.33% in Q4 vs 12.56% in Q3. Named as a FY27 growth leader.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Book grew 7% QoQ but net NPA was static at 2.76% vs 2.75%. Growth to be slower than the overall book, limited to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Mortgage / housing
segments.commentary: Housing yield 9.85% in Q4 vs 9.83% in Q3. Cited as a driver for growth in newer states.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending / BC model and FLDG cover?

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the NII margin expansion and CD ratio?

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income guidance?

rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA to INR110-115 crore and 21% margin but gave no revenue or occupancy guidance and deferred medium-term numbers to MUFG, with Agartala occupancy dipping and Raipur still loss-making at INR3 crore a quarter.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks flagged include Jamshedpur approval slippage to early FY28, Raipur ARPOB dilution (INR44,500 to INR42,300) from Ayushman Bharat mix, and Agartala occupancy at ~51% last month with doctor attrition ~10%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Recent launches (Dumdum cardiothoracic unit, Howrah MAKO knee programme, Agartala PET-CT and linear accelerator) are already live, and Raipur targets ~10 liver transplants a year in its first year, but no new named launch is dated.

rows.label: Raipur loss taper to operational breakeven
rows.why: Raipur Q1 loss INR3 crore and occupancy 17% vs 7% a year ago; management expects the loss to taper through FY27 toward ~30% exit occupancy, but breakeven is ~20 months out.

rows.label: Annual October tariff increase (inflation-linked)
rows.why: Tariff increases come every October and are described as a small contributor to ARPOB; no tariff hike was taken in Q1 FY27, and ARPOB is ~INR42,350 network-wide.

rows.label: Agartala recovery to pre-disruption international patient levels
rows.why: Agartala occupancy dipped (ALOS cut from 3.38 to 3 days, election curbs) and was ~51% last month, with management expecting a return to pre-disruption international patient levels in ~6 months and reaffirming the year-end target.

tone.note: Management was confident on case-mix-led ARPOB growth, the 21% FY27 margin path and Jamshedpur being on schedule, but cautious and deflecting on Agartala occupancy, Raipur ramp timing and Jamshedpur approvals, and declined medium-term occupancy or revenue guidance (deferred to MUFG).

544133|2026-03.headline: Exicom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 46% YoY to INR 388 crores and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR 0.3 crore for the first time since Tritium acquisition.
544133|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 282 crores with EBITDA of INR 29.9 crores (10.6% margin), driven by Critical Power (+23% YoY) and EVSE (+60% YoY). Consolidated revenue of INR 388 crores (+46% YoY) included Tritium, and consolidated EBITDA turned marginally positive. For full FY26, consolidated EBITDA was still negative at INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT was negative at INR 258 crores, with higher finance cost and one-time exceptional costs (VRS, Tritium retention, labour code). Management flagged a temporary inventory and receivables build as Hyderabad ramped up alongside Gurgaon.

financial_highlights.change: hit by finance cost, exceptional items, labour code

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 194 crores (consolidated ~INR 198 crores), up 23% YoY and ~18% QoQ; order book about INR 1,000 crores at 31 March. Exports hit a record ~INR 30 crores in Q4 (~15% of Critical Power sales vs ~10% historically).

segments.name: EVSE / EV charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Grew 60% YoY in Q4 and 40% for FY26; record quarterly EV charging revenue of INR 88 crores (management figure, basis not specified). Full-year EVSE consolidated growth 72%; Q4 consolidated EVSE +83% YoY.

segments.name: Tritium (US/Australia, EV charging)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about $10 million (sales $9.7 million), record order intake $10 million; EBITDA losses down about 30% QoQ. Management targets ~3x revenue and 25% lower EBITDA losses, with EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tritium: revenue to scale about 3x and EBITDA losses to fall about 25%; EBITDA breakeven targeted in Q4 FY27. Management said losses fall less sharply than revenue because low-cost acquired inventory is being used up, with margins normalising after about one quarter.
Exports: target to lift Critical Power export share to 20% in FY27 from ~10-15%.
Non-telecom BESS: internal target of over INR 50 crores business in FY26 from pilot-stage orders; management sees BESS possibly reaching ~30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years if successful.

Three Tritium products (TRI-FLEX inverter and two others) launching May-July 2026; management cites about INR 850 crores of combined FY28 revenue potential, subject to pilots. TRI-FLEX hyperscaler factory acceptance test ongoing, potentially $30-35 million FY28 revenue.
Gurgaon production to shift majority to Hyderabad over the next 2-3 months; inventory build expected to normalise over coming quarters.

Additional open opportunities of about INR 400 crores beyond the INR 1,000 crore Critical Power order book, including about INR 100 crores of new BharatNet tenders and about INR 150 crores of uncovered-village Phase-2.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant (newly inaugurated early March 2026) became fully operational in Q4 FY26 after Q3 trials; added depreciation is reflected in Q4 numbers.
Gurgaon plant still running; majority of production to move to Hyderabad over the next 2-3 months, with some production retained in Gurgaon.
Tritium manufacturing in Tennessee, US; R&D in Brisbane, Australia; Exicom R&D in Gurgaon (hardware) and Bangalore (software), with 130+ engineers.
Ring-topology PC charger: first pilot in Q4 FY26, mass production planned in FY27.
Exicom One: 80 sites executed in Q4 under this integrated products-and-services program.
demand_pricing: Critical Power pricing on BharatNet and other government contracts is fixed, so Q4 contribution margin was slightly below Q3 due to input cost increases from forex, commodities and geopolitical factors.
Management said large high-volume orders (e.g. a DC power system order above INR 100 crores with a leading Indian telco) help offset input cost inflation.
Standalone gross margin expanded to 27% on richer EVSE mix and fewer low-margin lithium battery sales.
EV demand: FY26 described as a record year with monthly EV sales above 200,000 across categories; electric car penetration cited as 5% and three-wheeler penetration 32%.

Competition noted in BESS and the market was described as large and competitive; BESS cell supply is import-dependent (China) until local cell manufacturing arrives, expected next year or the year after.

qa_highlights.question: What charging infrastructure is needed for commercial EV adoption and where is it happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is in fixed-route captive use such as ports, cement distribution and mining with 200-300 trucks; intercity commercial electrification is still about two years away.

qa_highlights.question: What is the product and revenue potential of the TRI-FLEX inverter and its applications?
qa_highlights.answer: TRI-FLEX converts grid power to high-voltage DC for DC microgrids, BESS integration and 800V data centres. A hyperscaler pilot is in testing and, if successful, could unlock significant FY28 revenue ($30-35 million cited).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company win customers for the two other new Tritium products in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said development was done with existing strategic customers, and it has line of sight to long-term contracts once pilots succeed.

qa_highlights.question: Does Exicom have OEM tie-ups for supplying chargers with vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Exicom is the largest home charger maker, with about a 50% chance a new EV in India comes with an Exicom charger, and it has OEM partnerships for home and fast chargers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS offering and its scaling path over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets commercial and industrial modular BESS, not utility, transmission, distribution or home. About 10-20 small projects were deployed in Q4, with an FY26 target above INR 50 crores, and BESS could reach about 30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years.

risks_watch: Consolidated FY26 EBITDA -INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT -INR 258 crores; breakeven depends on Tritium reaching 3x revenue and EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.
Tritium margin normalisation as low-cost acquired inventory is consumed after about one quarter.
Working capital: inventory build from parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad operations and higher receivables; collections and normalisation to be tracked.
Input cost inflation (forex, commodities, geopolitics) against fixed-price government BharatNet contracts.
Telecom tower installations slipped slightly in Q4; Critical Power demand depends on telco capex.
New Tritium products depend on hyperscaler pilot success and multi-month launch timelines (May-July 2026).
BESS cell supply dependent on imports until local cell manufacturing arrives.
544133|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, EVSE momentum and Tritium turnaround, while cautious on near-term Tritium margins, working capital and geopolitical or supply-chain headwinds. The CFO was less specific on the reasons for the full-year PAT loss and on receivables quality.
key_quotes: This reflects better product mix, sharper execution and Tritium beginning to scale commercially.
But we are firmly on our path for EBITDA breakeven at Tritium in Quarter 4 of FY '27 and the 3x revenue growth paved the way for it.
This is by design. We are stocking up both facilities to ensure smooth production continuity during this transition and to support an order book we are seeing in FY'27.

rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 10.6% in Q4 from 7.8% for FY26 and gross margin reached 27% on richer EVSE mix; Tritium EBITDA losses are targeted down about 25% in FY27 with breakeven in Q4 FY27, though fixed-price contracts and input cost inflation cap gains.

rows.why: No utilisation figure or new plant plan was disclosed; the Hyderabad ramp is already absorbing the Gurgaon shift, and BESS could reach ~30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years, so a further capex decision depends on that scaling.

rows.why: Consolidated FY26 EBITDA was -INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT -INR 258 crores; the path to breakeven depends on Tritium revenue rising about 3x and EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27, with input cost inflation against fixed-price BharatNet contracts and a working capital build.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.why: Exports hit a record ~INR 30 crores in Q4 (~15% of Critical Power sales vs ~10% historically) and management is targeting 20% export share in FY27.

rows.label: TRI-FLEX hyperscaler pilot, $30-35 million FY28 revenue
rows.why: Factory acceptance test is ongoing and the hyperscaler pilot could unlock $30-35 million of FY28 revenue, but this depends on pilot success.

rows.why: Management flagged a temporary inventory and receivables build as Gurgaon and Hyderabad ran in parallel; normalisation is expected over coming quarters but the CFO was vague on receivables quality.

tone.note: Management was confident on EVSE momentum, the Critical Power order book and the Tritium turnaround, and cautious on Tritium margins, working capital and input cost inflation; analysts pushed on the reasons for the full-year PAT loss and on receivables quality, which the CFO was less specific about.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.
544133|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 57% YoY to INR236.8 crore, with Critical Power up 80% to INR176 crore and EV up 15% to INR61 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR176-177 crore, up 73-80% YoY and down ~11% QoQ; BharatNet is among the largest contributors, with a 60% share in that project per management. Export sales about INR15 crore (~8% of Critical Power).

segments.name: EV Charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.name: Tritium (consolidated, US DC fast charging)
segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected within the next two quarters (management could not specify Q2 or Q3).
Tritium EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27, with 3x revenue growth versus last year targeted.
Standalone Critical Power exports targeted to rise from ~8% to ~15% of Critical Power sales within FY27.
AC charger monthly run rate expected to rise ~50% over the next three months.
Parallel-run fixed costs (~INR8.7 crore in Q1) expected to phase out as Gurgaon transition completes over coming quarters.
Tritium large strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX from hyperscaler) contingent on trial success.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and fully in production in Q1 FY27; management says it gives 3x production capability versus Gurgaon.
Standalone depreciation rose ~67% YoY, and management said standalone D&A increase was INR10-12 crore.
Management said DC charger utilisation is ~65% (90-100% for DC power system lines), AC charger ~100%, and PCBA and battery lines ~100%.
Ordered an additional AC charger line; management said the Hyderabad plant was built for ~2x AC capacity.
Tritium US factory capacity is about USD100 million a year versus ~USD10 million current quarterly revenue run rate (about one-quarter utilised).
demand_pricing: Critical Power order book ~INR1,000 crore; consolidated order book INR1,400 crore-plus as of 30 June 2026.
Large DC power system order of INR85 crore from a leading Indian telco; supply agreement with a large tower company for power systems and batteries.
BharatNet: INR700 crore open orders plus ~INR800 crore of service orders over 10 years; BSNL Phase 2 expected ~2,000 sites at INR90-100 crore.
BESS (commercial and industrial, mostly under 0.5 MWh): ~15 MWh orders worth ~INR20 crore in hand and ~34 MWh (INR45 crore) in advanced pipeline.
EV charger order book about INR200 crore for AC/DC chargers in India plus ~USD2 million export orders; 10 new export countries won; 15 new network operators added in Q1.
Margins on some large orders were hit by forex and commodity price increases, partly offset by volumes.
Supply disruptions in semiconductors, plastics and copper were cited as the main constraint, not capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated EBITDA swung from breakeven in Q4 FY26 to a INR22 crore loss in Q1; what drove the sequential drop and when does breakeven return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 seasonality in Indian business and Tritium's low-cost acquired inventory eroding, lowering Tritium margins. It still expects Tritium EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and consolidated breakeven within the next two quarters, without specifying Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Tritium's doubled order intake convert to revenue, and is the 3x growth and Q4 FY27 breakeven target still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the USD20 million backlog as of 1 July plus new bookings and large strategic wins (double-digit million dollars, executing from calendar 2027 Q1) give confidence in 3x revenue growth and Q4 FY27 EBITDA breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hyderabad plant utilisation and where will it reach in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad was built for about 2x AC charger capacity and roughly 4,000 DC chargers. Utilisation is about 65% on DC chargers, close to 100% on AC chargers, 90-100% on DC power system lines, and close to 100% on PCBA and battery lines. AC charger monthly run rate is expected to rise about 50% over the next three months, and another AC line has been ordered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV revenue mix and growth outlook, and why is the AC capacity figure inconsistent with the annual report (42,000 to 222,000 units)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of revenue, with mix expected to stay similar or rise slightly. Management said the 222,000 figure is right and that 48,000 was single-shift, with the doubling based on double-shift operation; it will revert with an exact answer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone depreciation rise, and what is the Tritium capitalisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone depreciation rose about 67% YoY to INR10.3 crore, with management attributing an increase of INR10-12 crore to the new plant. Tritium's higher depreciation reflects capitalised R&D and acquisition-related servicing costs, which management expects to be amortised over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can EV charger market share and unit volumes be estimated from EV registrations, and why was standalone EV growth only 15% when AC demand is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a very high share of wallbox chargers but not portable chargers, and volume depends on whether OEMs bundle wallboxes. Its DRHP cited 60% wallbox share, and it estimates current wallbox share at north of 50%. The 15% standalone EV growth reflects Q4 DC charger pull-forward; AC may have grown about 30% and DC about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US Tritium factory capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the US factory can service about USD100 million a year, about 2.5x the current ~USD10 million quarterly revenue, and it is running at about one-quarter of that today due to the ongoing turnaround.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven timing is not pinned down (Q2 or Q3 FY27), and Tritium breakeven is targeted only for Q4 FY27; the Tritium margin cushion from acquired low-cost inventory has already eroded.
Tritium strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX) are contingent on trial success and calendar 2026 conversion.

Working capital pressure from parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad operations: elevated inventory and receivables, plus ~INR8.7 crore of Q1 parallel-run fixed costs expected to phase out over coming quarters.

Shift in EV growth from DC to AC chargers and reliance on Q4 pull-forward; watch whether standalone EV growth accelerates beyond 15% YoY.

But on a consolidated basis, the breakeven may be over the next 2 quarters itself. I can't specify whether quarter 2 or 3.
Some of the challenges today is not capacity, it's supply chain disruption.
So I think it's just a timing issue. But this growth is not 1x. It's continuing.

544134|2026-03.headline: Platinum Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 132 crore, EBITDA up 95% to INR 15.3 crore; FY27 guidance above 40% revenue growth.
544134|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 132 crore (+37% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 15.3 crore (+95%, margin 11.6%, +350 bps) and PAT of INR 14.8 crore (+164%). Full-year consolidated revenue was INR 450 crore (+15%), but EBITDA (INR 59.8 crore, +4.2%) and PAT (INR 51.2 crore, +3.7%) grew far slower. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 40% and a 35% CAGR over FY26-29, with the Egypt plant slated for Q3 FY27 and oleo chemicals sales starting April 2026. Raw-material inflation from the March geopolitical events created a temporary margin pressure that management expects to pass through over time.

qa_highlights.question: How is FY27 40% growth split between India and Egypt, and how much is CPVC?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% of FY27 revenue from Egypt and the rest from India; CPVC expected to grow decently, with most growth from CPVC and lead-free products.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q4 gross margin pressure come from CPVC mix, and will margins bounce back in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 margins were about the same as Q3; the dip came from March raw-material price rises. Margins are expected to hold if raw materials stabilise, with a time lag in passing costs on.

qa_highlights.question: What is CPVC revenue and exit run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC revenue was about INR 110 crore of INR 450 crore in FY26; monthly run-rate ranges INR 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are CPVC gross margins versus the blended average?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC gross margin was 6-7% at launch and is now 18-20%, with management suggesting it could rise a further 2-4 percentage points as a commodity product.

qa_highlights.question: What is the oleo chemicals revenue plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales started April 2026; FY27 target INR 55-60 crore, reaching run-rate by Q2; own plant to follow in about 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs jump and what senior hiring occurred?
qa_highlights.answer: Employees rose from about 120 in FY25 to about 150 now and about 170 in April 2026, plus senior hires to stabilise management; employee cost to sales up about 1 percentage point, expected to normalise once the new plant runs optimally.

qa_highlights.question: What is Egypt's breakeven and margin profile?

qa_highlights.question: How did pipe demand look in July and August, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pipe demand degrew in Q1 across pipe companies, picked up from August, and is expected to stay good through December as PVC prices stabilised and turned upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Oleo sales in Q1 FY27 and can the segment reach INR 55-60 crore by year-end?

qa_highlights.question: When will CPVC margins recover toward 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC margin is about 18% now and management targets 20-21% by Q4 FY27. Recovery depends on demand, since supply currently exceeds demand, and on local raw material sourcing, which is adding cost.

qa_highlights.answer: Lower sales-related expenses, since the company skipped exhibitions in Q1, and lower ECL provisions offset the drop in contribution margin, leaving EBITDA margin impact negligible. Lead-free PVC offtake was lower, which hurt mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation of the existing stabilizer capacity and the threshold to sustain margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The expanded plant was fully operational only from 21 May 2026, so utilisation is expected to be around 30-35% in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
