544210|2026-03.headline: Emcure FY26 revenue crossed INR9,204 crore (+16.6%), but Q4 domestic growth slowed to 5.2% on Zuventus disruption; FY27 guided to low-to-mid-teen growth.
544210|2026-03.overview: Emcure reported FY26 revenue of INR9,204 crore (+16.6% YoY), with adjusted PAT up 41% to INR1,008 crore and EBITDA margin up 80 bps to 19.4%. Q4 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,470 crore, but domestic growth slowed to 5.2% because of attrition and restructuring at the newly consolidated Zuventus business. International markets grew 25.7% in Q4, with Europe and Canada leading. Management said April is on plan and guided FY27 to low-to-mid-teen revenue growth and 75-100 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY; margin up from 18.4% in Q4 FY25
Up YoY due to Manx payouts and Zuventus minority stake buyout

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR4,027 crore (+10%), led by women's health, cardio, CNS and oncology. Q4 revenue INR977 crore (+5.2%) was hit by Zuventus. Management said ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% and the full-year ex-Zuventus base growth was high single digit.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR5,177 crore (+22.2%). Q4 revenue INR1,493 crore (+25.7%); currency added roughly 7-8% overall, about 11-12% in Europe.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,850 crore (+25.5%). Q4 revenue INR538 crore (+35.8%), helped by Manx and Amphotericin B. Management expects mid-teens CAGR over the next two years.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,487 crore (+18.7%). Q4 revenue INR399 crore (+28.6%), driven by market share gains and launches.

segments.commentary: FY26 ROW revenue INR1,840 crore (+21.8%), with ARV and non-ARV both contributing. Q4 emerging markets revenue INR556 crore (+15.5%).

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Zuventus impact on India growth and whether restructuring will weigh on the next few quarters.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year ex-Zuventus base growth would have been 9-10%, and Q4 ex-Zuventus was below 8%. It expects the impact to fade, with April back on track.

qa_highlights.question: What operational synergies are expected from Zuventus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing synergies are limited because the plants serve different products. Gains are expected in sales and marketing organisation and support functions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 domestic growth outlook and the currency assumption behind guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth is expected at 8-9% and Emcure aims for low double digits. The guidance assumes INR92/USD.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raw material and geopolitical cost pressure is in guidance?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Quebec partnership with Dr. Reddy's aims for an early launch around Q2 FY27, and its own filing will target the rest of Canada in the medium term. Deal terms were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is organic growth but in-licensing will continue where it is accretive.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps for FY27 reiterated.

544213|2026-03.headline: Aelea Commodities H2 FY26 standalone revenue Rs 189.50 cr with 13.10% EBITDA margin and Rs 12.35 cr PAT; FY26 revenue up 112% to Rs 363.12 cr.
544213|2026-03.overview: Management reported H2 FY26 standalone revenue of Rs 189.50 cr, EBITDA of Rs 24.82 cr (13.10% margin) and PAT of Rs 12.35 cr (6.52% margin), versus losses a year earlier. For FY26, standalone revenue rose 112.07% to Rs 363.12 cr, EBITDA was Rs 40.20 cr (11.07% margin) and PAT Rs 21.19 cr, with EPS of Rs 10.40 versus Rs 0.65. Consolidated FY26 revenue was Rs 381.50 cr (up 109.46%) and PAT Rs 21.32 cr. The call was dominated by a 10-year (FY37) strategy presentation, with the Q&A focused on higher finance costs, working capital and inventory build, CNSL plant timing, and FY27 guidance, which was not quantified.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone revenue from operations, H2 FY26

financial_highlights.change: Compared with losses in the corresponding period last year

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations, H2 FY26

segments.name: Cashew kernel processing (core)
segments.commentary: Processes raw cashew nuts (RCN) into wholes and pieces; average mix 63% wholes and 37% pieces, with average kernel realisation of about Rs 590-595/kg. Around 16,000 tonnes of RCN processed in H2 and a similar volume in H1. About 95% of raw material is African-origin, sourced via merchant traders.

segments.name: CNSL / by-products (oil extraction, solar)
segments.commentary: CNSL extraction facility of above 50 MT is under construction, with management guiding to benefits from around H2 FY27 and a product-level EBITDA margin of about 10%. Rooftop solar is installed; ground-mounted solar awaits government approval. B2C consumer pouches are about 1% of sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27: management expects top-line and bottom-line growth at rates similar to FY26, but declined to give a revenue number; an analyst's Rs 500 cr FY27 revenue figure was not confirmed.
FY28: too early to comment; management said it will revisit after about six more months of work.
EBITDA margin: management says the company normally operates at around 10-11% EBITDA margin, which it says it has broadly met.
Finance cost: management expects it to stay at similar or higher levels as the company deepens its value chain, and said absolute figures will grow with scale.
CNSL plant: construction nearly complete with about 30 days of works remaining; commissioning depends on government approvals. Phase 3 capex is expected later in the year.
B2C: targeted at roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin in the long run, pursued through a product basket rather than e-commerce.
capex_capacity: Capacity scaling from 40 MT/day to 140 MT/day, which management says is backed by IPO proceeds; current utilisation about 94-95%.
Phase 2 (CNSL) capex is already committed and underway, with only a small amount pending; Phase 3 capex is expected in the later part of the year.
Ground-mounted solar is pending government approval because of changes to norms for consuming solar power; rooftop solar is complete.
Long-term 2037 strategy targets 1,000 MT/day cashew capacity, plus almond, walnut, pistachio and makhana processing (makhana with a 50-tonne capacity plan).
A Maharashtra cultivation project and capex was flagged by an analyst as not updated; management said it is still being worked on and not crystallised.
demand_pricing: Management said processing is constrained by raw-material quality rather than machine capacity; the company says it fully used its enhanced capacity during H2.
Raw-material sourcing has moved deeper into the value chain (direct sourcing at about 60-65%), which lifted margins but raised working capital and finance costs.
Geopolitical disruption: longer sea transit from Africa, currency swings of around 50 paise a day, and higher RCN price volatility, with no material price impact yet.
Institutional clients are a stated priority for longer-term visibility, but institutions are about one-fifth the size of general trade in the market.
Inventory rose to about Rs 100 cr and management expects it to increase further with growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 8 cr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company moved deeper into the value chain, where suppliers do not give credit, but margins are better. Finance cost is expected to stay at similar or higher levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 and FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be similar to FY26 in rate, with no numbers given. FY28 comment deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNSL plant timeline and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction nearly complete with approvals pending; benefits expected around H2. Management said CNSL adds EBITDA rather than top line, at about 10% product-level EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and RCN volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 94-95%. About 16,000 tonnes of RCN were processed in H2, roughly the same as H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix between Africa and India?
qa_highlights.answer: About 95% of processing is African-origin, sourced through merchant traders based in Singapore or Dubai, and 5% is local.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2C strategy and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C is about 1% of sales. Management said it will grow organically rather than through heavy marketing, targeting roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin on a product basket.

risks_watch: Working capital and finance cost: rising short-term borrowing and inventory (about Rs 100 cr) as sourcing deepens; management gave no debt-to-equity red line.
CNSL and ground-mounted solar commissioning depends on government approvals, which have no fixed timeline.
Geopolitical and shipping disruption from Africa, with longer transit and higher currency and RCN price volatility.
Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 numbers; watch whether growth matches the stated similar rate.
Related-party or structural details on the Maharashtra project remain unclear and not yet crystallised.
544213|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the 10-year strategy and FY26 results, but evasive on forward numbers: it repeatedly declined to give FY27 or FY28 figures, the Maharashtra project and timelines, and it deflected on B2C sales and the cause of higher finance cost.
key_quotes: So, for FY27, we are likely to continue our growth rate.

At the end of the day, it's cashew and you, me, or whoever goes at buying it would like to see what is the per gram, per 100 gram price and compare it with wherever you are, other source of buying is.
So we have roughly 95% of the entire processing depending on the African origins only.

rows.why: Management says it normally runs 10-11% EBITDA margin and broadly met it (FY26 standalone 11.07%, H2 13.10%), with CNSL adding about 10% product-level EBITDA margin from H2 FY27, but higher finance cost and direct sourcing (60-65%) offset gains.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 growth at a rate similar to FY26's 112% revenue growth, but gave no number, and volume is constrained by raw-material quality rather than machines, with ~16,000 tonnes RCN processed in both H1 and H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: Phase 3 capex later in FY27 (within next 2-3 quarters)
rows.why: Utilisation at 94-95% with the Phase 2 CNSL capex committed, and management says Phase 3 capex is expected later in the year, so a new capex announcement is likely.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: B2C is about 1% of sales and targets 13-15% EBITDA margin via a product basket, while the 2037 plan adds almond, walnut, pistachio and makhana (50 t plan), but no launch date is given.

rows.label: Direct sourcing deepens value chain (60-65%)
rows.why: Direct sourcing at about 60-65% lifted margins but raised working capital and finance cost, with inventory at about Rs 100 cr expected to rise further with growth.

rows.label: Ground-mounted solar and CNSL approvals
rows.why: Ground-mounted solar awaits government approval over solar-norm changes and CNSL commissioning depends on approvals, with no fixed timeline.

rows.label: Working capital and finance cost build
rows.why: Finance cost went from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 8 cr and management expects it to stay similar or higher as inventory grows past Rs 100 cr.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 10-year strategy and FY26 results (H2 PAT Rs 12.35 cr) but declined to quantify FY27/FY28, the Maharashtra project, and timelines; analysts probed finance cost, working capital, inventory and CNSL timing.

544222|2026-03.headline: Akums Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 61.6% YoY to INR152 crore (13.1% margin), with FY26 revenue up 5.8% to INR4,359 crore.
544222|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,158 crore, up 9.7% YoY and flat QoQ, while adjusted EBITDA reached INR152 crore, driven by CDMO profitability and trade generics turning EBITDA positive. Reported Q4 PAT of INR81 crore was held down versus the prior year by a large deferred tax asset benefit in the base; PBT rose to INR121 crore from INR75 crore. FY26 PAT fell to INR256 crore from INR344 crore, which included a INR106 crore DTA benefit in FY25. Management guided to double-digit CDMO volume growth in H1 FY27, a sharp narrowing of API losses, and a Zambia supply contract of about $25 million per year from Q2 FY27.

vs INR344 crore in FY25, which included INR106 crore DTA benefit
+61.6% YoY vs INR94 crore; +3.3% QoQ vs INR147 crore; margin vs 8.9% in Q4 FY25 and 12.7% in Q3

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,485 crore (+8.6%) and EBITDA INR467 crore (+2.9%). Q4 revenue INR952 crore (+13.4% YoY, +4% QoQ) and EBITDA INR137 crore (+54.9% YoY, +9.1% QoQ); management cited operating leverage from better utilisation and newer facilities.

segments.name: Domestic branded formulations (Akumentis)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR446 crore (+2.9%) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+17%). Q4 revenue INR102 crore (-1.5% YoY, -11.1% QoQ) and EBITDA INR22 crore, flat YoY and down 13.2% QoQ.

segments.name: International branded formulations
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR143 crore (flat) and EBITDA INR36 crore (+32.3%). Q4 revenue INR36 crore (-9.7% YoY, -28.5% QoQ) and EBITDA INR10 crore (+14.7% YoY); Q4 margin around 28%, helped by marketing investment and about 3.5-4% gross margin uplift from forex gains.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR100 crore (-13.2%) and EBITDA negative INR10 crore vs negative INR28 crore. Q4 revenue INR27 crore (+22.6% YoY) and EBITDA positive INR1.4 crore, first positive quarter versus negative INR3 crore in Q3.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR184 crore (-15.9%) and EBITDA negative INR40 crore vs negative INR44 crore. Q4 revenue INR41 crore (-18.8% YoY, -24.9% QoQ) and EBITDA negative INR12 crore, against negative INR6 crore in Q4 FY25 and negative INR7 crore in Q3.

guidance_outlook: CDMO: double-digit volume growth expected in Q1 and Q2 FY27; management declined to guide on Q3/Q4 pricing or full-year revenue and gave visibility of 45-60 days of the revenue book.

Zambia: about $25 million (roughly INR230 crore at current rates) of annual supplies from Indian facilities in FY27 and FY28, expected to start by end Q2 FY27 at margins similar to CDMO; supplies cease after FY28.
European CDMO contract: about EUR35 million per year on a MAT basis from launch through 2032, fixed-price; management expects margins similar to CDMO or in the high teens.
Akumentis: expected to grow at or above IPM rates, targeting low-double-digit growth; exports expected to grow double digits in FY27.

API: losses expected to fall sharply in FY27 but full-year EBITDA may still be negative; monthly EBITDA-positive is a goal to be assessed over a couple of quarters. European audit of API facility expected in the upcoming quarter.

Tax: effective tax rate about 32% currently, with 29% to be built into the model; normalising towards 25% depends on loss-making API and trade generics turning profitable. FY27 capex target INR300 crore vs INR222 crore in FY26.
capex_capacity: Plant 2 received EU GMP accreditation in January 2026; dossier filings and country registrations under way in multiple European markets, with commercial supplies targeted from FY28.
Plant 3 received ANVISA approval in FY26 in addition to European GMP approval; the injectable facility is ANVISA approved and a separate oral liquids facility is EU GMP approved.
New injectable facility utilisation is in the early teens; management expects significant ramp-up during FY27.
Oral solids facility expansion has started because volumes grew about 20% plus over two quarters; part of the FY27 capex of INR300 crore is for this.
Zambia local plant: total investment about $45 million, 51% borne by Akums; revenue from the local facility expected from calendar 2029.
Haridwar land lease executed to add land for capacity expansion, utilities and support.
demand_pricing: CDMO volume growth in H2 FY26 was led by existing customers with existing brands, from in-house production switches and other CDMOs; management says it is broad-based.

API prices fell about 20-25% as a basket over FY26, then rose by single-digit percentages after the post-war geopolitical situation, but remain below April 2025 levels; management does not expect a sharp fall from current levels.
CDMO pricing is a percentage markup on input cost, so absolute gross profit moves with API prices; the business is pass-through for raw material cost.
Domestic formulations took very little price increase in FY26 and focused on volume; management expects this to change, with double-digit top-line growth in domestic formulations targeted.
Trade generics scaled down from about INR400 crore in FY22 due to elongated working capital; it is now kept at similar revenue and EBITDA levels.
GLP-1: management is still evaluating entry timing, API partners and dosage forms, citing volatile and falling prices.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth above 25% in the last two quarters: what drives it and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is from existing customers and existing brands, not new geographies, and management expects double-digit growth to continue into Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3.5% negative price variance reverse as API prices rise, and can CDMO grow at double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: API prices are up single-digit percent but still below April 2025; management believes they will not fall sharply from current levels and sees H1 volume growth as the driver.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current effective rate is about 32% due to loss-making entities; management plans for 29% overall and expects a move toward the normal rate once API and trade generics are profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR222 crore; the FY27 target is INR300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a FY27 top-line target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year FY27 revenue target.

qa_highlights.question: How is the European contract structured and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an established product, fixed-price through 2032 and priced at current API levels, with about EUR35 million per year on a MAT basis and margins similar to CDMO or in the high teens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zambia contract's duration and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Supplies of $25 million a year in FY27 and FY28 from India; a local plant with about $45 million total investment (51% Akums) to start revenue in calendar 2029.

qa_highlights.question: How is cash to be deployed, given the 18% payout and large cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities are oral solids capacity expansion and inorganic niche acquisitions, including branded portfolio deals, though management said current brand valuations are high.

risks_watch: API losses: FY26 EBITDA was negative INR40 crore for a third straight year; the European audit of the API facility and the pace of loss reduction are key to watch.
Raw material inflation from crude-linked solvents and the Middle East situation; management says CDMO is pass-through, but absolute margins fall when input prices fall.
Working capital days rose to 105 from 91, driven by inventory build and advance payments to creditors.
Effective tax rate of about 32% versus the 25% normal rate, which weighs on PAT conversion.
Newer injectable facility utilisation is in the early teens; ramp-up in FY27 needs to show.
Schedule M implementation impact on customer mix was not addressed by management.
key_quotes: So we expect that while the full year would still remain negative, this will be sizably lower and would have a significantly lower drag on our P&L.
No ma'am, we do not want to answer this question. We don't want to state future numbers.
So this is for two years, $25 million each FY27, FY28.
I will like to skip this question because honestly, we have no visibility on ground of how the government plans to roll this out.
544222|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on CDMO volumes, Zambia, the European contract and Plant 2/3 approvals, but cautious and evasive on API pricing, FY27 revenue targets and tax timing. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 top-line number and said Q3/Q4 CDMO pricing would be addressed next quarter, and it deferred on Schedule M rollout and GLP-1 entry timing.

544222|2026-06.headline: Akums Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to INR1,167 crore and EBITDA 35.4% to INR175 crore, led by CDMO volumes and API prices.
544222|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue reached INR1,167 crore (+13.9% YoY, +0.8% QoQ) and operating EBITDA INR175 crore (+35.4% YoY), with margin at 15.0%, up 238 bps YoY. PAT rose 56.1% YoY to INR101 crore. CDMO carried the quarter with 18.6% revenue growth and higher capacity utilisation, while domestic branded (Akumentis) and international branded formulations were muted on EBITDA, the former due to a ~200-person field force addition. Management reiterated 14-15% annual margin guidance and said it could lean to the upper end, and announced the Oriflame India manufacturing acquisition.

+35.4% YoY; margin +238 bps YoY, up from 13.1% in Q4 FY26
+56.1% YoY; +24.1% QoQ vs Q4 FY26 INR81 crore
Management stated no debt; net worth above INR3,400 crore

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR964 crore (+18.6% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) on volume growth and higher API prices; EBITDA INR163 crore (+36.8% YoY), aided by better capacity utilisation.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR115 crore (+7.3% YoY, +12.9% QoQ); EBITDA INR12 crore (-25.4% YoY, -46.5% QoQ) due to field force expansion of ~200 people (~15%).

Annual EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%, with management inclining to the upper end given strong Q1.

API: monthly EBITDA-positive target by end of February/March 2027; annual profitability from FY28.

No subcontracting planned; management says low-margin portfolio will not be rationalised as gross margins remain above 40%.

Unosource (international) muted in Q1; management expects order growth from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a time frame to evaluate exiting the API business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a question of a U-turn; the focus is on improving profitability, with quarterly losses declining over the past two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zambia timing and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue expected from Q3 and some of Q4; about USD 25 million (roughly INR240 crore) in FY27; margins expected in the higher teens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed about INR1,600 crore is net of debt; 98% is in fixed deposits with nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Oriflame deal capability or capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a niche formulation play that adds skin care capacity and enables entry into colour cosmetics, building on R&D strength.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic sales-force productivity below industry and why add MRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is in a build phase, with the MR addition targeting new geographies and headquarters, and that productivity will rise toward industry averages as the business scales.

544223|2026-03.headline: Ceigall Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 30.5% YoY to INR1,294 crores; FY27 guidance is minimum 15% revenue growth and 11-12.5% EBITDA margin.
544223|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest execution quarter of the year, with standalone revenue of INR1,294 crores (up 30.5% YoY) and standalone EBITDA of INR183 crores (14.1% margin). Full-year standalone revenue grew 14.3% to INR3,869 crores, while FY26 order inflow of INR11,332 crores far exceeded the INR5,000 crore guidance, taking the order book to INR18,554 crores. Management guided FY27 to at least 15% revenue growth, 11-12.5% EBITDA margin and at least INR5,500 crores of order inflow. Working-capital stretch (trade payables and unbilled revenue days both up sharply) and a large pending equity commitment for HAM and renewable projects were the main analyst focus, alongside the INR13,000 crore Romania bid.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone revenue from operations Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: vs INR109 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR585 crores at 14.6% margin / INR309 crores at 7.7% PAT margin

segments.name: Road EPC and HAM (NHAI, MPRDC)
segments.commentary: Order book comprises 19 EPC projects, 10 HAM projects and 1 DBFOT project; all HAM projects are NHAI except one MPRDC project. Sahebganj-Areraj-Bettiah corridor (INR2,160 crores project cost) is the largest award to date.

segments.name: Renewable and power transmission
segments.commentary: Renewables are 19% of the order book across 7 projects; FY26 inflow was about 35.02% renewable. Solar and BESS awards include Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh solar projects, Morena BESS and the Velgaon 400 KV substation.

Morena BESS project awarded but not started: PPA not yet signed and transmission line tender not yet received; work depends on government land, transmission connectivity and PPA.
Velgaon 400 KV substation in Maharashtra in progress; transmission orders placed and T&D construction underway.

Sobha project in Dubai (about AED250 million) was also bid.
NHAI pipeline about INR2 lakh crores per management; company is bidding projects above INR2,000 crores and has a INR21,160 crore project and a INR600 crore Zirakpur bypass project.
Escalation clause changed from quarterly to monthly by MoRTH; billing plan eased to monthly payments after the recent war-related notifications.

qa_highlights.question: Pipeline for domestic and international business, and targets over one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Offices opened in Singapore and Dubai, and a CEO International appointed. International expansion was slowed by the war; the company will bid abroad only if EBITDA margins and concessional IRRs are adequate.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue guidance of 15% looks low given the order book; what is the internal target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative; it had previously guided 10-15% and achieved it, and 15% minimum is intended as an easy-to-achieve floor.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and working capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: MoRTH notifications moved billing from milestones to monthly payments; more than INR400 crores from NEO asset sales is expected, so management says cash flow is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payable days jump from 79 to 138 and unbilled revenue days from 94 to 133?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to March billing being paid by the department only in April, with creditor payments linked to receivables; about INR300 crores was paid to creditors in April. Unbilled revenue rose because milestone billing on large projects (10% per milestone, over INR100 crores each) lagged, and should improve with monthly billing.

qa_highlights.question: Margin drivers in Q4 and risk from iron ore and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 margin was helped by four HAM projects started last year and higher turnover. Management said escalation is now paid monthly, so cost increases are passed through to the EPC contractor.

qa_highlights.question: Margins falling over three years as per the presentation slide 41?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said pure-operations EBITDA has stayed at 11-12.5% for three years; the earlier-year figures included bonus and royalty income (INR20 crores in FY25 and a Karnal-Pehowa bonus in FY24), which are included in revenue from operations.

qa_highlights.question: Equity investment needs and funding sources?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,937 crores is needed over three years (about INR800 crores renewable, rest HAM roads). Management cited unencumbered cash of about INR166 crores and FDR of about INR75 crores at March 31 (corrected from figures stated on the call), plus cash accruals and NEO proceeds.

risks_watch: Receivable and unbilled-revenue days rose sharply (unbilled 94 to 133 days; trade payables 79 to 138 days); watch whether monthly billing reverses this in coming quarters.

Large Romania bid (about INR13,000 crores) would be a major international entry and could be about 65-70% of the current order book; bid timing is uncertain and management said bid validity is nearing expiry.
Renewable projects depend on government land, PPAs and transmission connectivity; Morena BESS has not started.
HAM monetisation timing: only the Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali deal is binding, and the other two sales remain at non-binding offer stage.
Margin guidance of 11-12.5% is excluding other income, which management said is volatile; FY26 standalone PAT margin was 7.9%.

544223|2026-06.headline: Ceigall Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 10.2% YoY to INR901 crore, with EBITDA margin at 13.4% and order book at INR18,568 crore.
544223|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 10.2% YoY to INR901 crore and PAT rose to INR75 crore (8.4% margin) from INR56 crore. Consolidated revenue grew 15.7% to INR970 crore. The company completed its first HAM divestment (Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali) and started three new projects, while management kept FY27 margin guidance of 11-12.5% and raised revenue growth guidance to at least 15%. Q1 order inflow was modest at about INR600 crore against a INR6,000 crore full-year target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Northern Ayodhya bypass execution fall to about INR42 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said progress is steady and milestones are being met early; payment is only received on milestone achievement, and rain over the last 1.5 months affected timing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rewa solar project timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: PPA and land are in place; the transmission line tender has been floated and the company expects it soon, after which the project can start quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What equity will be invested in HAM and solar in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 balance commitment INR859 crore (INR310 crore solar, INR550 crore HAM); FY28 INR744 crore (INR296 crore solar, INR444 crore HAM). Initial equity at IPO was INR253 crore; total now INR692 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was margin higher than guidance and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Three new projects started in Q1 and more are starting; the CFO said FY27 margin guidance of 11-12.5% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation and other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation fell due to assets sold in the prior year on WDV method; other income fell as royalty is no longer charged and IPO-linked FD interest ended. About INR320 crore in FDs now earn interest, and management expects this run rate to continue.

544224|2026-03.headline: Afcom Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87.8% YoY to INR191.88 crore and PAT to INR44.66 crore, on war-driven charter demand.
544224|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR191.88 crore (+87.8% YoY), EBITDA of INR74.08 lakh per the call (+51.52%), and PAT of INR44.66 crore (+72.85%) under Ind AS. Full-year revenue was INR587.72 crore (+143.86%) and PAT INR121.90 crore (+230.05%), with PAT margin of 20.74%. Growth was driven by stranded-cargo charters after Middle East disruption in March 2026, with 415 of 602 Q4 trips being pure charters. Fleet expansion is the key near-term constraint: a third aircraft is operational, with fourth and fifth expected before the next quarter and wide-bodies (Boeing 777) planned from late 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +72.85% YoY; GAAP PAT was INR46.32 crore

segments.name: Dry lease (aircraft-plus-crew charter/scheduled cargo)
segments.commentary: Q4 dry lease revenue INR160.49 crore; FY26 INR528.71 crore on 1,923 trips and 24,353 tons, with 1,129 pure charters (about one-third in Q4).

segments.name: Q4 operating metrics
segments.commentary: Q4 average revenue per trip USD29,295.64 and yield USD2.72/kg versus FY yield USD2.54/kg; cost per kg USD1.84 in Q4 versus USD1.58 for FY. Weekly trips per aircraft averaged 23.42 in Q4 and 19 for FY.

guidance_outlook: Fourth and fifth Boeing 737-type aircraft expected to be operational before the next quarter (Q1 FY27), per management.

Two Boeing 777 wide-body aircraft: one expected operational in the last quarter of FY27 (per the call's timing), with the full four-777 plan expected to be fully operational by mid/second half of calendar 2027.

Management called a 777 revenue of about 3x a 737-800 at 14-15 rotations/month and 75% load factor, implying roughly INR75 crore/month per 777 as a conservative estimate; management said FY27 revenue could be at least double FY26 on existing resources.
ATF pass-through via fuel surcharge; designated carrier status cuts fuel-related VAT, adding about 5-7% benefit to overall fuel cost from the next financial year.
Maintenance reserve now expensed to P&L under Ind AS; management says no further fundraise needed for the fleet plan after QIB and preferential issues.
capex_capacity: Three aircraft in operation: VT-AFO, VT-AFN and the newly inducted third aircraft (VT-AFJ per Q&A), with the third aircraft held for a fresh C-check and contracted Middle East flying from late June.

FY26 capacity utilisation 81.42% on gross weight basis; utilisation hours per aircraft per day peaked at 11.45 (VT-AFO) and 10.51 (VT-AFN) in Q4 versus industry best 10-14 hours and Asia Pacific average 7.9.
Lease-related liability: three aircraft ROU assets INR306 crore, total lease liability INR338 crore, current lease dues INR49 crore plus INR16.1 crore lease finance cost over 12 months.

Funding: QIB and preferential allotment (INR200 crore each per analyst) stated to cover wide-body induction; fourth and fifth aircraft costs largely covered, with customs and minor expenses remaining.
demand_pricing: March 2026 saw a sudden capacity withdrawal from Middle East carriers; Q4 month-end revenue ran about INR42-44 crore per month, with March about 22-23% above the Jan-Feb average.

Management said April and May demand remained above average but below March panic levels; fuel prices (ATF) at INR2,24,000/KL were offered at INR1,69,000/KL under designated carrier status, versus INR85,000/KL before.
Q4 yield USD2.72/kg versus IATA industry average cited at INR222/kg; management said company yield per kg is better than the IATA average.
Chennai international cargo grew 12.5% YoY in FY26 versus 5.4% all-India, per management's data.
Over 60% of billing is in USD. Receivables about 60 days on recent billing (IATA norm 45 days); management said no receivables older than 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for fourth, fifth and wide-body aircraft induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Third aircraft operational; fourth and fifth to be operational before next quarter; one 777 targeted in last quarter of FY27, with four 777s in total per management's later clarification, fully operational by second half of calendar 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of ATF price surge and pass-through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is passed through 100% via fuel surcharge; the market absorbed the April spike, which tapered in May and June; designated carrier status yields a fuel price benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 yield only USD2.72/kg despite higher freight rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher charter share (415 of 602 Q4 trips) and short-sector stranded-cargo flights lowered yield per kg; more weight-based cargo would have raised yield.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of 777 aircraft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 777 can do 14-15 rotations per month at 75% load factor, giving about 3x a 737-800's revenue; an analyst's estimate of about INR75 crore per month per 777 was described as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Ind AS adjustments, particularly a large forex loss charged to P&L, and maintenance reserve now expensed.

qa_highlights.question: Ideal FY27 revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resources would at least double FY26 revenue on a conservative basis; no numerical guidance given.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility (ATF up sharply from April) and dependence on a fuel surcharge pass-through; pricing could soften if the Middle East disruption ends.
Revenue dependence on temporary war-driven charter demand; management acknowledged yields hardened in March and the sea-freight alternative is also rising in cost.
Ind AS restatement now shows large forex losses and maintenance reserve charges, which compress reported margins; Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3.
Tax liability: about INR33 crore of FY26 current tax outstanding per analyst; management acknowledged only partial advance tax payment and promised improvement.
Aircraft induction delays (fourth, fifth and 777 timelines) and third aircraft utilisation; aircraft tracking data disputed by management.
Disclosure gaps: cargo-type revenue breakdown (ODC, general, hazardous, perishables) and Nauru JV/MRO details not provided pending UPSI considerations.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to at least double FY26 (FY26 INR587.72 crore), which is conservative per management, but it is unquantified and depends on the Middle East disruption persisting.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Boeing 777 wide-body induction (about INR75 crore/month per 777 as a conservative estimate) is planned, with one in the last quarter of FY27 and four fully operational by H2 CY27.

rows.label: Fuel surcharge pass-through and designated-carrier VAT benefit
rows.why: Fuel is passed through 100% via surcharge, and designated-carrier status is expected to cut fuel cost by 5-7% from the next financial year.

rows.label: Contracted Middle East flying from late June

rows.label: Receivables and tax outflow
rows.why: Receivables run about 60 days vs the IATA norm of 45, and about INR33 crore of FY26 current tax is outstanding per an analyst after only partial advance tax payment.

tone.note: Management was confident on fleet expansion, 777 economics and FY27 doubling of revenue, but evasive on routes, Nauru details and timelines, citing UPSI; analysts pushed on tax liability, Q4 margin decline and aircraft count inconsistencies.

544225|2026-03.headline: Ola Electric Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin rose to 38.5% and first positive operating cash flow (Rs 91 crore CFO), but revenue was low on depressed deliveries.
544225|2026-03.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as a reset quarter: gross margin reached 38.5% (33.5% excluding PLI) versus 13.7% a year earlier, and consolidated OpEx including leases fell to Rs 428 crore from Rs 844 crore. Revenue was weak because deliveries were depressed by internal service and operations fixes, with FY26 consolidated revenue at Rs 2,253 crore on 173,794 deliveries. Management says registrations have recovered for three months, orders are running ahead of registrations, and Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders and Rs 500-550 crore revenue. The Gigafactory's first 3 GWh is in ramp-up with the remaining 3.5 GWh slated for June, and the company is pushing Shakti and Roadster bike growth.

segments.commentary: 2.5 GWh operational, with 6 GWh installation largely complete; commercialisation of the full 6 GWh expected by end of Q1 FY27. Still in investment phase, with cell CapEx for 6 GWh essentially done apart from payouts in Q1-Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said March registrations were about 10,000 and April about 12,000, with May trending 14,000-15,000; Q4 revenue was low because operations were being fixed and volumes restarted only mid-March, with production backlog spilling into Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from current volumes to the 20,000 units/month breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebound should reach about 17,000-18,000 units per month including about 15% bikes; better service stability and inventory availability could take volumes to 20,000-22,000 over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Advantage of own cells versus imported cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Own cells are already cheaper on pure BOM even at low volumes; at 6 GWh with overheads the advantage is expected to be 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not advertise in print media, and is the Rs 2,000 crore cell monetisation progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Company prefers word-of-mouth and does not do TV or IPL sponsorship; may advertise in coming months. Cell monetisation requires a subsidiary-level capital raise; management has inbound PE interest but gave no timing beyond 'in due course'.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time ASP change and will prior quarters be restated?
qa_highlights.answer: Extended warranty packages moved from upfront to deferred revenue recognition after discussion with auditors, a Rs 20-30 crore impact already baked into published numbers; no restatement of prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 CapEx, R&D and cash burn outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto maintenance CapEx about Rs 50 crore per year, PPE CapEx below Rs 50 crore; cell CapEx for 6 GWh essentially complete; R&D mid-single-digit % of revenue; operating cash burn Rs 300-500 crore in FY27, turning positive after 20,000-25,000 orders per month.

qa_highlights.question: Status of solid-state and sodium-ion cell technologies?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are at lab scale; focus is on ramping 46-series NMC, with an LFP cell to start ramping in the factory next quarter; solid-state and sodium to be commercialised as the industry matures.

qa_highlights.question: Why are service issues linked to parts unavailability, and why NMC for Shakti?
qa_highlights.answer: Parts were not stocked at service centres and procurement was reactive (20-30 day fulfilment); now stocked locally and procured on forecasts. Shakti uses NMC today and will move to LFP next quarter; Shakti ramp is slower because NMC 46-series goes to Auto.

risks_watch: Volume recovery must reach 20,000-25,000 units per month for adjusted EBITDA breakeven; Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders versus registrations trending at 14,000-15,000 in May.

Bike EV and Roadster ramp and new product launches (Mahashakti, LFP Shakti) depend on supply and timing; an Analyst Day is planned in one to two months.
Margin sustainability: management flagged short-term commodity pressure and aggressive growth investment in the last month or two.

544225|2026-06.headline: Ola Electric Q1 FY27 deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units, Auto revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), Auto gross margin 30.5%.
544225|2026-06.overview: Ola returned to volume growth in Q1 FY27, with deliveries of ~39,200 units (nearly 2x QoQ) and orders of ~44,000, while electric two-wheeler registrations grew 97% against a market up ~17% QoQ, lifting share from 5.1% to 8.4%. Auto revenue rose 72% QoQ to ₹455 crore with gross profit of ₹139 crore and Auto gross margin held at 30.5%. Consolidated opex fell 22% QoQ to ₹333 crore (including a ~₹55 crore one-time reversal of a Cell ACC PLI penalty provision), and adjusted operating EBITDA improved to –₹195 crore from –₹326 crore in Q4 FY26. Management pivoted Auto distribution from company-owned to a multi-channel model with dealers, with the first batch slated to go live on Janmashtami (4 September), and reiterated a Cell gigafactory ramp to 6 GWh.

First Mahashakti MoU with Axis Energy for 20 GWh over 5-6 years; early Mahashakti revenue hoped for Q3 or Q4.

544226|2026-03.headline: FirstCry Q4 FY26: consol revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr for FY26; Q4 adjusted EBITDA up 18% to ₹118.7 Cr amid India gross margin pressure.
544226|2026-03.overview: Brainbees (FirstCry) reported Q4 and FY26 with consolidated FY26 revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr, adjusted EBITDA up 24% to about ₹486 Cr, and free cash flow positive for the full year. India multi-channel grew 11.4% in Q4 but gross margin fell on diaper price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal players, plus a transitory manufacturing hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs. Management says the offline channel grew about 15% in Q4 after a product-mix shift, and that RocketBees and Qwik delivery initiatives are lifting service levels, with the benefit expected to show in FY27. International losses fell 35% in FY26 and GlobalBees core categories grew 28%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% and FY26 revenue +9%; GMV +11% in FY26, crossing $1 billion for the first time. Management says the segment stayed PAT and cash flow positive in FY26. Non-diapering is over 85% of GMV; diapering (about 15% of business) faces heavy price competition.

segments.name: International (UAE and KSA)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue above $100 million, growing about 10% in FY26; Q4 revenue +9%. Gross margin rose 240 bps for FY26 (470 bps in Q4). Management did not give a timeline for reaching break-even.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: FY26 consolidated revenue +20% (organic, after brand rationalisation) and core categories +28%. Adjusted EBITDA post-corporate expenses was 5.8% of revenue in Q4 (₹26.5 Cr) and about 3% for FY26 after ESOP cost. Brand rationalisation is expected to finish by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Others (preschool)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue +11% with EBITDA margin about 27% (vs 24% in FY25). Preschools more than doubled from 208 at end FY24, and enrolled students are almost 3x in two years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India multi-channel GMV and revenue growth guided to be much superior to FY26; management expects sequential quarterly improvement to continue.
India multi-channel FY27 EBITDA (rupee terms) guided to grow double digits, per management's 'should' answer; margin expansion expected outside diapering.
Gross margin loss from the Q3 diaper competition (about 140 bps) expected to take 4-6 quarters to reverse; manufacturing-related loss expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 via pass-through.
Company-owned and FOFO stores: about 100 openings planned in FY27 after pausing COCO openings in FY26 (10 COCO stores added in FY26).
Qwik expected to reach roughly 10% of total B2C online shipments over FY27; RocketBees already at 40%+ of online delivery volume, with a target of 45-50% by mid-2026.
Continued international loss reduction in FY27; management aims to take losses to zero as early as possible.
capex_capacity: RocketBees own-network coverage grew from 13 cities (Q2) to 22 (Q3) to 62 cities (Q4); management aims to cross 50 cities by next quarter-end.
Qwik quick-delivery pilot began 1 Dec 2025 and now runs in 5 cities; it delivers in under 3 hours and is already over 20% of online orders in the covered catchments.
Logistics cost front-loading of about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until RocketBees and Qwik networks mature.

Offline initiative (width-to-depth product assortment change) went live in Q4 FY26 and drove about 15% offline GMV growth.
Management says on-time delivery exceeds 92%.

Q4 online GMV grew about 10.5%, and online growth held at about 11-12% across all four quarters of FY26. Offline GMV grew about 15% in Q4.

India multi-channel Q4 orders +10% and GMV +12%; AOV in International is about 4x India's.
Management says the Middle East has seen some moderation in consumer sentiment and import complexities, but it is 'beyond anyone's control'.
Ages 6-12 is the fastest-growing age cohort in India multi-channel.

qa_highlights.question: What share of orders now goes through FirstCry's own delivery network, and what is the logistics cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Share rose from about 28% at end Q3 to over 40% at end March 2026, with a target of 45-50% by mid-year. Logistics cost is front-loaded by about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until networks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company pause COCO store openings in FY26, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings were paused for capital efficiency given macro conditions. Management plans about 100 stores in FY27 across COCO and FOFO formats, citing the best offline growth in seven quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin pressure in diapering split between competition and input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The 140 bps Q3 competitive hit has continued into Q4. The remaining manufacturing-related hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs is transitory and expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 as prices are passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the online growth slowdown structural, given offline grew faster than the 11% overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Online GMV grew about 10.5% in Q4 and 11-12% through FY26. Management expects RocketBees and Qwik to lift online growth in FY27, with results lagging. Product mix between online and offline has not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Can India multi-channel EBITDA grow double digits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing recovery of the manufacturing hit by Q2 (three quarters of benefit), continued margin expansion in the non-diaper categories, and operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East situation affecting international revenue and break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer sentiment has moderated and import complexities have emerged. Management sees this as an opportunity to optimise discounting and marketing and to improve home-brand mix, and says the focus remains sustainable growth over top-line chasing.

risks_watch: Diaper price war from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms could keep gross margins under pressure beyond the 4-6 quarter window management has given.
Management has tied the FY27 recovery to a Q2 pass-through of manufacturing costs, with rupee depreciation and crude prices as the swing factors.
Middle East consumer sentiment and import complexities could slow International, where revenue growth was about 9-10%.
Online growth has run at about 10-12% and needs to accelerate in FY27 for the stated guidance to hold.
GlobalBees brand rationalisation is due to finish by end Q1 FY27; the consolidated growth figure will lag until then.
Management declined to quantify AI-driven savings, saying the number will come in later quarterly updates. It also said there have been no buyback or acquisition discussions.

544226|2026-06.headline: Brainbees Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell ~260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
544226|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, with GMV up 12% to ₹2,807 crore and AUTC up 10% to 11.8 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin dropped to 36.5% from 38.5%, mainly from India multi-channel diapering competition and manufacturing cost pass-through lag. Management said diapering competition is easing and that the crude/rupee cost pass-through completes by end-Q2, but gave no firm timeline for margin recovery. Growth drivers cited were RocketBees (over 50% of online shipments), FC Qwik (125,000 shipments in June across 12 cities) and offline GMV growth of 15%.

segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY, best in seven quarters; GMV +12%, orders +12%, AUTC +10%. Non-diapering is ~85% of GMV; gross margin down ~260 bps YoY and EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY on diapering competition and manufacturing input costs. Remains PAT positive.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% YoY, AUTC +7%, GMV +9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced 22% YoY; loss-to-revenue improved from 10% to 7%. Management targets EBITDA neutrality but gave no timeline.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat due to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand, expected to complete in Q2 with growth recovering from Q3. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% from 1%.

segments.name: Preschool (FirstCry Intellitots)
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA +65% to ₹5 crore. Over 500 preschools; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years, organically, with no M&A being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Jay Laddha asked how much of the manufacturing-related gross margin loss was recovered in Q1 and whether International breakeven timing or FY27 guidance had any update.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India multi-channel gross margin recovered about 20 bps of the 280 bps Q4 drop, with full pass-through of crude and rupee costs by end-Q2. On International, Abhinav Sharma declined to give a breakeven quarter, pointing to inputs (home brand mix, high-margin brand curation, quality customer acquisition); the loss-to-revenue ratio moved from -16% in March 2025 to -7% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Kumar asked whether India multi-channel growth can be sustained next quarter and when margin will recover.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to remain elevated for the next few quarters on RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline stores. Margin recovery is expected faster than the 4-6 quarter diapering normalisation, with diapering competition easing in July and August and crude/rupee pass-through complete by end-Q2, full recovery likely from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Ranodeep Sen asked about the company's right to win in diapering against pharmacy and private-label entrants, and whether M&A is being considered in preschool.
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goel said diapering retention is hard for private labels and that quick commerce discounting is temporary; branded diapering showed some improvement in Q1. Supam Maheshwari said FC Qwik and the full-destination model support retention. On preschool, he said organic growth to at least 1,000 preschools over a couple of years, with no M&A being looked at yet.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked whether the sequential India multi-channel EBITDA margin decline is due to crude-linked inflation and whether H2 EBITDA margin will at least match last year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 280 bps Q4 drop had two components: diapering competition (expected to take 4-6 quarters to normalise) and manufacturing input costs (full recovery by end-Q2, normalised from Q3). Gautam Sharma bridged the 290 bps YoY India EBITDA margin decline as 260 bps gross margin loss plus 30 bps from logistics costs, partly offset by marketing and fixed-cost leverage. Supam Maheshwari said the 280 bps gap should 'dramatically' reduce, without a quantified target.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked why India revenue growth (18%) exceeds GMV growth (12%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the revenue line combines online, offline and manufacturing, while GMV is at MRP. GST 2.0, effective Q2, reduced MRP and contributed to the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Gokal Gandhi asked for the profitability delta between diapering and non-diapering and the company's share of the diapering category.
qa_highlights.answer: Supam Maheshwari said the delta between diapering and non-diapering has widened, with over 50% of GMV in fashion and over 50% of business in home brands. He said the delta should shrink as diapering margins recover; no market share figure was given. Archana Menon asked about store expansion and non-diapering consumables; management said about 100 net new stores in FY27 (90-100 per Gautam Sharma, net of attrition) and that non-diapering consumables are about 15% of GMV with healthy margins.

544227|2026-03.headline: Unicommerce FY26 revenue rose 51.6% to INR204.3 crore, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA growth slowed to 7.8% as investments step up.
544227|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 51.6% to INR204.3 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 54.5% to INR43.9 crore, with FY26 being the first full year consolidating Shipway. Q4 revenue grew 14% YoY to INR51.6 crore, but adjusted EBITDA grew only 7.8% to INR9.6 crore and PAT grew 1.6% to INR3.4 crore after management began stepping up growth investments in Q4. Management guided to lower adjusted EBITDA and PAT over the next two quarters, while expecting higher full-year operational profitability in FY27 than FY26. Management also disclosed it is evaluating a merger with Shipway Technology Private Limited.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth now relies on new clients and new product adoption as market growth softened; price escalation was added to new contracts from last year and will be extended to existing contracts with benefits in later years.

qa_highlights.question: What is NRR and the incremental sales and marketing spend?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company rely on acquisitions for growth, and what is the target profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions are a core strategy: targets should be relevant to existing customers, AI-relevant, profitable or near profitability, and reasonably valued. Pre-purchase (ConvertWay adjacency) and post-purchase (analytics, loyalty) are white spaces.

qa_highlights.question: How is ESOP expense rising and what dilution should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ESOPs were issued to existing and new mid-to-senior talent, increasing share-based expense; it aims to avoid dilution from acquisitions by using cash instead.

qa_highlights.answer: India business has seen little disruption; the Middle East, a small contributor, saw slightly longer sales cycles in recent weeks, which management said are normalising.

544238|2026-03.headline: Premier Energies FY26 revenue rose 20.7% to INR8,026 crore and PAT 61.1% to INR1,510 crore, with order book at INR14,010 crore (+66% YoY).
544238|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR8,026 crore (+20.7% YoY) and PAT of INR1,510 crore (+61.1% YoY), with operational EBITDA margin of 30.4% and PAT margin of 18.8%. The 5.6 GW Sitarampur module plant is complete and expected to reach full ramp-up in about two months, and the Transcon 51% acquisition is closed. Capacity is set to rise to 16.75 GW by July 2026, with FY27 capex of INR5,100 crore. Management guided to no specific margin numbers, citing rising cell, silver and freight costs, and said it would pass silver risk to customers on new orders. The K-Solar acquisition was dropped, and the company is pursuing an inverter JV with SMA SGS as first preference.

segments.commentary: TOPCon cell line commissioned June 2025 is running at 90%+ utilisation; average TOPCon efficiency about 25.5%. Cell market pricing stable at 13.5-14 US cents per watt per management. Cell capacity to rise to 10.6 GW shortly, with a 7 GW cell line due in two tranches (4.8 GW June, 2.2 GW September).

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Module capacity 11.1 GW; management says utilisation is about 75% (roughly 7-7.5 GW). The 5.6 GW Sitarampur plant uses about 40% less manpower per MW than existing plants. Management expects DCR share to rise every quarter.

segments.name: Transcon (EPC/transformers, HV/EHV)
segments.commentary: Acquired 51% stake; FY revenue INR423 crore and PAT INR45 crore. Plant due for completion in July 2026; management says it has secured some first orders, and ramp-up is expected to take about two years.

segments.commentary: Inverter business pursued via a JV with SMA SGS (first preference) after K-Solar deal lapsed. BESS capacity pace is deliberately slowed due to imports at about 11% duty; localisation policy expected around FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Cell costs rose to about 6-6.2 cents from 3.5 cents, passed through on non-DCR modules. DCR margins are maintained through scale and mix. Glass cost unchanged; aluminium (about 11% of module cost) rose slightly, offset by design changes.

544238|2026-06.headline: Premier Energies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR2,508 crores, PAT up 53% to INR472 crores at an 18.8% margin.

The 5.6 GW Seetharampur module plant is operational, while the 7 GW TOPCon cell line is in late commissioning with trial runs expected later in August. Order wins were INR3,011 crores in the quarter, taking the total order book to INR15,000 crores including transformers. segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR110 crores, PAT INR18 crores; management expects business to roughly treble over three years, with transformer capacity going from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28. Last year's revenue was about INR400 crores.

544239|2026-03.headline: ECOS Q4 FY26 revenue up 16.65% to INR2,067.6 million, EBITDA down to INR241.5 million; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth at 11-13% margin.
544239|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 16.65% YoY to INR2,067.60 million, while EBITDA declined to INR241.53 million from INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25, reflecting continued investment in people, technology and leadership. For FY26, revenue rose 23.58% to INR8,081.58 million and EBITDA was INR939.29 million, with margins hit by higher manpower cost, tech spend, ETS price competition and a one-time doubtful-debt provision of about INR80 million. Management said the Middle East crisis dented CCR growth in March, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and EBITDA margin of 11-13%, with cost growth expected to be lower than revenue growth. Analysts pressed on margin compression, falling revenue per trip and competitive pricing in ETS; management attributed the trend partly to shorter trips and airport transfers.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25 (decline)
vs 4.04 million in FY25, approx. +29% YoY

segments.name: ETS (employee transportation services)
segments.commentary: 58% of FY26 revenue and 57% in Q4 FY26. Stable demand from IT/ITES and a strong surge from GCC clients, but competitive pricing pressure was most visible here.

segments.name: CCR (chauffeur-driven car rental)
segments.commentary: 42% of FY26 revenue and 43% in Q4 FY26. Growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, though management says it bounced back; management described CCR as a brand-led business with a premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth aspiration of 18% to 20%; management expects about 60-65% of growth from new client acquisition and the rest from existing clients.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 11% to 13%, with management saying this holds for the next couple of years too.
Employee cost growth budgeted at about 13% to 16% in the latest AOP; other expenses to rise about 8% to 9%.
Fuel price increases above roughly 5% are generally passed through to clients, with lags of a few days to a few weeks.
No dividend declared; the board will hold a separate meeting to consider dividend or other ways to enhance shareholder value.
capex_capacity: FY26 vendor partner network of about 20,000 vehicles, versus about 14,000 in FY25; the model remains asset-light.
Over 14% of CCR corporate bookings came through CabDrive Pro, API or the customer app in Q4 FY26.
Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides, aimed at premium individuals and SMEs rather than mass B2C.
New core backend platform launched to improve process efficiency.

EV investment remains cautious; capex would rise materially only if EVs become financially sustainable and charging infrastructure and residual values support them. Analyst noted about INR120 million capex over four years (about INR30 million a year).
demand_pricing: Active client base above 1,750; 223 new clients added in FY26 (64 in Q4) versus 188 in FY25.
55% of FY26 revenue from clients associated with ECOS for more than five years. Churn among top 200 clients is about 2-3%, per management.
Demand from GCCs and manufacturing facilities is a notable driver of ETS enterprise wins; CCR growth is diversified across sectors.
Competitive price pressure is mainly in ETS, led by new entrants; management says prices should rise once operations prove unsustainable.

Average revenue per trip fell from about INR1,600 in FY25 to about INR1,550 in FY26, versus about INR1,750-1,780 in FY24. Management cited pricing pressure plus shorter ETS trips and more CCR airport transfers.
No demand impact seen yet from the government's work-from-home appeal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the West Asia crisis affecting demand, and what is FY27 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CCR growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, with a bounce back expected if the disruption is short. Management aspires to 18-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can fuel price hikes be passed on, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Most contracts have pass-through clauses triggered above roughly 5%, with lags of days to weeks. Management says the 6-7% increase has been fully passed on.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR8 crore receivable provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal proceedings for recovery are ongoing and management is hopeful. Recovery may come in FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected growth rates for employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is budgeted to grow about 13-16% and other expenses about 8-9%, both below the revenue growth target. Management expects operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue per trip declining, and is pricing pressure easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ETS pricing pressure and shorter trips plus airport transfers. Pressure appears to have stabilised in the last quarter, while the company is also winning larger enterprise contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to the earlier 14-16% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% for FY27 and the next couple of years. It expects CCR brand premium to offset ETS price competition over time.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin in FY26 was about 11.6%, down from roughly 15% at IPO, and Q4 EBITDA fell YoY despite 16.65% revenue growth.
Falling revenue per trip (about INR1,550 in FY26) indicates pricing pressure in ETS from new entrants.
Pending legal recovery of the roughly INR80 million doubtful debt; timing is uncertain.
Middle East and fuel-price volatility affecting CCR demand and the lag in fuel pass-through.
Cost growth versus revenue growth in FY27: the company needs to deliver operating leverage against its 13-16% employee cost budget.
Dividend decision pending a separate board meeting.

Management was candid that pricing pressure in ETS and the March CCR slowdown weighed on the quarter, and it avoided quantifying the timing of margin recovery beyond guidance.

rows.why: Management only aspires to 18-20% FY27 revenue growth, and margin guidance of 11-13% is below the earlier 14-16% range with ETS price competition still in place.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR241.5 million from INR264.7 million despite 16.65% revenue growth, and revenue per trip slid to about INR1,550 from about INR1,600, with the Middle East crisis having dented CCR growth in March.

rows.why: Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides and a new core backend platform launched, but no further product launch dates were given.

rows.why: Legal recovery proceedings are ongoing and management is hopeful, but the roughly INR80 million provision may only be recovered in FY27 or later, so timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Operating leverage from cost growth below revenue growth
rows.why: Employee cost is budgeted at 13-16% and other expenses at 8-9% against 18-20% revenue growth, with fuel increases above about 5% passed through to clients with lags of days to weeks.

tone.note: Management was confident on client wins, GCC-driven ETS demand and the CCR brand premium, and cautious on near-term margins, the March CCR slowdown and EV capex. Analysts pressed on margin compression (FY26 about 11.6% vs roughly 15% at IPO), falling revenue per trip and ETS pricing competition.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.
544239|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 16.7% YoY to INR2,113.72 million and trips rose 27% YoY to about 1.48 million, with 61 new clients added. EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

qa_highlights.question: What changed since the 11-13% margin guidance, what is driving pricing pressure, and at what margin will the company walk away from business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition and pricing pressure were higher than anticipated, especially in ETS. It has set internal client-level thresholds below which it will not bid, and did not disclose a level; company-wide margin is expected to be held at around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost savings and productivity be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Automation of CCR contact centre, dispatch, billing and booking, expected mainly to reduce employee expense and improve vehicle utilisation; management said it would also negotiate harder with vendors. Savings were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge given low entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three elements: long-standing enterprise relationships, a large reliable vendor supply base built over decades, and processes and people. It said the market is only 15-20% organised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins decline and how low can they go?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower rates given to win business are absorbed partly from vendor margins, most evident in ETS. Management declined to specify a floor but said it has internal thresholds.

qa_highlights.answer: No timeline given; management said it is guiding to maintain margins because competition duration is uncertain, with operating leverage expected at a much larger scale (over INR 1,000 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said costs are shared across the organisation, so a segment EBITDA split is not practical to provide.

544240|2026-03.headline: Raymond Lifestyle FY26 total income hit record INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA rose 23% to INR804 crore; Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore.
544240|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a recovery year, with record annual total income of INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA of INR804 crore (11.4% margin, +23%). Q4 FY26 total income was a record INR1,810 crore (+15% YoY), with EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore and margin up 210 bps QoQ to 8.4%. The company remains debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR179 crore, and net working capital days fell from 87 to 77. Management labelled FY27 a "Year of Consolidation", guiding to double-digit top-line and bottom-line growth without numeric EBITDA guidance.
