544240|2026-06.headline: Raymond Lifestyle Q1 FY27 total income rose 6% to INR1,560 crore, EBITDA up 11% to INR135 crore at 8.6% margin, net cash surplus INR154 crore.
544240|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 6% YoY to INR1,560 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR135 crore, with margin up 40 bps to 8.6%. Garmenting was the standout, with revenue up 50% to INR296 crore and EBITDA turning positive at INR22 crore. Branded Apparel grew only 4% and Branded Textiles fell about 2%, mainly on base effects and adverse channel and product mix. Management called FY27 a year of consolidation, with net store closures continuing for two to three more quarters, and said Q1 was ahead of budget.

financial_highlights.change: vs net debt INR55 crore in June 2025, INR209 crore swing
-15 days vs 90 days in Q1 FY26
Attributed to business mix shift toward lower-margin garmenting
Includes INR11 crore one-off lease-accounting item per management

segments.name: Branded Textiles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR684 crore vs INR699 crore YoY on base effect from a large prior-year fabric quarter; EBITDA INR95 crore vs INR107 crore, margin 13.9% on scale deleverage.

segments.name: Branded Apparel (four core brands)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR349 crore, +4% YoY, with LFS and e-commerce growing high double digits (LFS above 25%); EBITDA INR18 crore, margin 5.1% on adverse channel mix.

segments.name: Garmenting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR296 crore vs INR197 crore, +50% YoY on US tariff rationalisation and new UK/EU clients; EBITDA INR22 crore vs negative INR8 crore, margin 7.3% vs -4.1%.

segments.name: High Value Cotton Shirting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR195 crore vs INR205 crore YoY on base effect; EBITDA steady at INR19 crore, margin 9.7% vs 9.1%.

segments.name: Emerging Businesses (Ethnix, Raymond Home, innerwear, Chairman's Collection, sexual wellness)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR79 crore, +9% YoY; now reported as a standalone segment after reclassification. Ethnix net stores down 17 in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management is bullish on FY27 and said Q1 is ahead of budget phasing and ahead of last year; Q2 described as decent.
Garmenting capacity is full through December; orders booked from January onwards. Management said no risk to margins on cost-plus contracts, though changes in Sep-Oct could affect pricing.
Price hikes to start in Q2: management estimates 5-7% in apparel and 7-9% in fabric, calibrated against volumes.

Medium term: aim to at least double turnover in five years and grow EBITDA faster than revenue, before any Kearney-led transformation outcomes. Mid-teens ROCE described as the endeavour, not a target. Garmenting EBITDA double-digit described as an endeavour with no firm timeline.
Net branded EBO openings to be negative in FY27; EBO closures expected to take another 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Garmenting: five factories (three in Karnataka, one new in Andhra Pradesh, one in Ethiopia); no spare capacity until December per management. Company has 11 factories in total.
Active network 1,627 stores across 600 cities. Since June 2025, 133 stores exited and 85 opened.
Branded EBOs in Q1: 8 opened, 24 closed (net -16). TRS format net +6. Ethnix: 1 opened, 18 closed (net -17). Management said EBO network is down 34 net (9%).
Renewable energy share in factories around 12% this year vs 8-9% last year; target 25% by 2030, which management expects to reach early.
Ethnix plan: shift sherwanis and bandhgalas above INR50,000 to made-to-measure; basic kurtas to be sold through TRS and e-commerce; high-impact flagship stores in wedding areas.
demand_pricing: Garmenting US share fell to 55% under tariffs and has recovered to 59-60%; UK rose from 10% to 12% and Europe from 6% to 7-8%. Management aims to bring US to about 55%.
New clients named: El Corte Ingles (Spain), OVS (Italy), Carl Gross (Germany), T.M. Lewin (UK, shirting). UK FTA live from 15 July; EU FTA expected to take 6-9 months to take effect.

Branded apparel: management attributed the weak quarter to Adhik Maas (about one month without auspicious buying) and delayed festive dates by 20-25 days. Casual brands (ColorPlus, Parx) growing double digit; casual share in Park Avenue and Raymond Ready-to-Wear reached about 18%.
Retail: TRS stores up 5-6% and EBOs up 3% like-for-like. Management said premium-end off-take in Q1 was not an issue.
Raw material inflation YoY: wool about +100%, cotton and flax about +20%, chemicals about +30%. Gross margin was held despite this because Q1 sold at forward-booked prices.

qa_highlights.question: Input cost pressure in fabric and textiles, and how price hikes or inventory efficiency will offset it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited wool, flax, cotton, dyes and chemicals as rising costs. Mitigation includes new vendors, Make in India sourcing, freight consolidation, and a cost transformation project. Price increases to begin in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Garmenting outlook and whether contracts allow pass-through of RM costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders are cost-plus, and bookings for January onward are open with December capacity full. Higher plant utilisation is expected to help margins. Management declined to give firm double-digit EBITDA guidance, citing unpredictable international trade conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation rise of about 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR11 crore was a one-time lease-accounting error from last year and will not recur, so it can be excluded from run-rate depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Store rationalisation timeline and Ethnix store additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Closures will take another 2-3 quarters, so FY27 net branded EBO openings will be negative. Ethnix will shift top-end products to made-to-measure and move basic lines to TRS and e-commerce, with flagship stores in wedding areas.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue, margin and ROCE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to at least double turnover and grow EBITDA faster than revenue in five years, before any Kearney-led project outcomes. Mid-teens ROCE is described as a good outcome for a manufacturing business, not a target.

qa_highlights.question: Which brands drive casualisation, and what are the branded apparel and export order trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Branded apparel grew 4% due to EBO closures, with e-commerce and LFS growing high double digits. Order books span Europe, US, Japan, Korea and Asia. Management said FY28 is not being looked at closely.

risks_watch: Store closures: management says EBO closures need another 2-3 quarters, with FY27 net branded EBO openings negative; monitor net EBO count (down 34, about 9%) and whether closures stay on this timeline.

Raw material inflation: wool about +100%, cotton and flax about +20%, chemicals about +30% YoY; Q1 margins relied on forward-booked prices, so Q2 onwards depends on price hikes of 5-7% in apparel and 7-9% in fabric holding volumes.

Garmenting visibility: capacity full through December with bookings from January; management declined firm double-digit EBITDA guidance, citing unpredictable US tariff and Middle East developments, and Sep-Oct cost moves could affect cost-plus pricing.
Branded apparel: revenue +4% YoY and EBITDA margin 5.1%; recovery relies on festive and wedding dates shifting 20-25 days into H2, with Adhik Maas hitting Q1 suit off-take.

Depreciation normalisation: exclude INR11 crore one-off lease-accounting item from run-rate; watch depreciation and ROCE, which management said will take time to improve as stores and capacity are added.
Ethnix repositioning to made-to-measure and high-impact flagships; watch whether the 17-store net reduction and shift in channel translate into profitability.
key_quotes: So my guess is that our H2 will be very, very strong.

But if you ask me, I have done enough businesses in my life to know mid-teens is a good ROCE to have for a manufacturing -driven business, so that will be the endeavor, but that is not the target that I am chasing.
So the endeavour is the same, to keep improving on this till the tailwinds persist.
We have closed taking orders for December on 31st July.

544244|2026-03.headline: Gala Precision FY26 revenue rose 32% to INR314 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.51% on a ~1% (INR3.23 crore) forex loss.
544244|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR95 crores (up 26% YoY), with EBITDA of about INR17 crores (up 31%, margin 17.57%) and net profit of about INR12 crores (up 22%, PAT margin 12.9%). For FY26, revenue reached INR314 crores (up 32%), EBITDA INR52 crores (up 27%, margin 16.51%), and profit after exceptional items INR36 crores (up 32%). Management attributed the annual margin dip mainly to a forex loss, and said raw material costs are passed through to customers with a lag. The Chennai fastener plant reached a Phase 1 run-rate of about INR5 crores per month, with Phase 2 expected to add capacity by mid-2026.

segments.name: DSS (disc spring)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 49% of FY26 revenue, described as a stable recurring base.

segments.name: SFS (special fastening solutions)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crores, reaching INR108 crores in FY26 (+64% YoY); about 34% of revenue and fastest growing, with fasteners sales of about INR100 crores.

segments.name: CSS (coil spring)
segments.commentary: About 17% of FY26 revenue, supported by steady industrial and mobility demand.

guidance_outlook: Company growth target of 20% to 25% in overall revenue; wind segment fasteners and springs targeted at 25% to 30% in the short term.
Chennai FY27 sales expected at about INR80 crores (67% to 70% of INR120 crores capacity); capacity to reach INR10 crores per month by end of FY27.
Cash flow guidance: maintain or improve cash-flow conversion by about 10% YoY; inventory days at 103, with a target to cut about 10 days.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise in the 17% to 19% range by FY27 end, assuming no further forex volatility.
Export share expected to stay at 35% to 40% of sales.
Offshore wind expected to contribute about 10% of fastener sales within two to three years.
EU-India FTA expected to take effect around January 2027, removing the 3.7% EU import duty, though CBAM may offset the benefit.
Wada land (5 to 10 acres) expected to be finalised around June-end or July 2026; new plant build of 15 to 18 months; FY27 capex about INR50 crores, funded by internal accruals and bank borrowings.
capex_capacity: Chennai fastener plant: installed capacity 4,600 MT; Phase 1 reached about INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annualised) from August 2025 ramp-up; plant utilisation about 35% in FY26.
Chennai Phase 2 capex to complete by June-July 2026, adding another INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annual); total Chennai capacity INR120 crores per annum by year-end.
Wada plant: no additional land; disc spring running about 80% utilisation; coil spring and fastener capacity have headroom, to be unlocked via productivity, line balancing and outsourcing.
Wada land purchase of 5 to 10 acres under negotiation for an own-land expansion; Chennai backup option is a SIPCOT long lease or an existing building to shift stud manufacturing.
Renewable and mobility capex: 1.8 MW open access solar plant ordered for captive consumption.
demand_pricing: Wind: about 60% to 65% of wind sales from India and 30% to 35% from exports; first high-tensile bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India from Chennai in Q4 FY26.
Growth mix in FY26 cited as about 10% from new customers, 10% to 12% from new parts with existing customers, and 5% to 7% organic growth.
Addressable market expanded: studs cover about US$1 billion; bolts and nuts take it to about US$2.5 billion. Global fastener market cited at about US$100 billion.
CSS competitors named as NHK Spring and Stumpp Schuele & Somappa; some imports from Europe remain a substitution opportunity.
Raw materials are 100% passed through to customers; process costs (gas, diesel) are being repriced from April 2026, with recovery expected on an annualised basis.
Hedging policy cut from 70% to 40% of estimated export collections, covering 12 months, net of imports for USD exposure.
Management says a currency depreciation gave a top-line benefit in Q4 but also created a non-cash forward-cover loss; the amount was not quantified on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What wind-energy order book and growth visibility exist for the coming year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 25% to 30% growth in short-term wind fasteners and springs; wind sales are about 60% to 65% India and 30% to 35% exports.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chennai revenue ramp and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 ramped from INR1 crore to INR5 crores per month from August; Phase 2 adds INR5 crores per month by June-July, with INR80 crores targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall to 16.5%, and how is raw-material inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop from about 17.1% mainly to a roughly 1% (INR3.23 crore) forex loss, not mix or raw materials; raw materials are fully passed through with a lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a land and expansion plan beyond Chennai?
qa_highlights.answer: Wada land (2 to 3 plots) is in advanced talks, likely finalised June-end or July; a 15 to 18 month build is expected, with about INR50 crores of capex in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the EU-India FTA and CBAM matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Current EU import duty of 3.7% on Gala products would fall to zero when the FTA takes effect around January 2027, but CBAM could offset the benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and export mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Forward cover is set at up to 40% of estimated export collections for 12 months; exports are expected to remain 35% to 40% of sales.

risks_watch: Forex volatility: a forex loss of about INR3.23 crores hit FY26 margins, and forward-cover losses can distort quarterly profit.
Chennai utilisation: FY26 was about 35%; the FY27 target of about INR80 crores depends on Phase 2 commissioning by mid-2026 and on scaling the bolt business.
Inventory: Chennai ramp-up adds inventory; working-capital days (103) and cash conversion are a watch item.
Wada land acquisition timelines could slip; Chennai backup plan depends on a SIPCOT lease or an existing building.
Pending patent suit on wedge lock washers: next hearing in June 2026; no arguments yet.
CBAM and EU trade changes could offset the expected FTA duty benefit.
Raw-material and gas cost pass-through is lagged; quarterly margin volatility is possible before price revisions take effect.
544244|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity plans, with specific timelines. Cautious and hedged on land acquisition and on quarterly forex and cost pass-through effects. Several answers were loosely worded, and exact figures (such as the currency benefit to revenue) were deferred.
key_quotes: And now we are seeing the similar runway as of now we will going to have in April, May, June.
So, we are quite close to in closing this land, but still not close, that is the fact.
So, with combination of this all, we are seeing that the current year whatever number we are targeting, we should be able to optimize our capacity utilization in Wada.
On the annualized basis, we will definitely see that whatever is been incurred is recovered.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chennai Phase 2 capex is under construction to add INR5 crores/month (about INR60 crores annual) by June-July 2026, taking total Chennai capacity to INR120 crores p.a., though Phase 1 utilisation was only about 35% in FY26.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 20-25% overall revenue growth (midpoint 22.5%), wind fasteners and springs 25-30%, and Chennai FY27 sales of about INR80 crores (67-70% of INR120 crores capacity) versus about 35% utilisation in FY26.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: next 2-3 quarters (Wada land finalisation June-end or July 2
rows.why: Wada disc spring runs at about 80% utilisation with no additional land, and management guided about INR50 crores of FY27 capex for a 5-10 acre own-land plant once land is finalised; timing depends on land negotiations.

rows.why: Management guided only 20-25% revenue growth and a 17-19% EBITDA margin band, with no sign of running ahead of these targets.

rows.why: First high-tensile wind bolt supply to a global OEM in India started in Q4 FY26 and offshore wind is targeted at about 10% of fastener sales within two to three years, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Exports held at 35-40% of sales with wind exports at 30-35%
rows.why: Management expects exports to stay at 35-40% of sales, with wind sales already 30-35% exports and a first global OEM bolt supply started in Q4 FY26.

rows.label: Process-cost repricing from April 2026
rows.why: Gas and diesel costs are being repriced from April 2026 with recovery on an annualised basis, and raw materials are 100% passed through with a lag, which should support margins once revisions take effect.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth targets, Chennai Phase 2 timing and wind orders, but cautious on Wada land timing, forex and lagged cost pass-through, and deferred exact figures such as the currency benefit to revenue; analysts pressed on margin dip drivers and land timelines.

544244|2026-06.headline: Gala Precision Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ~INR75 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA margin 16.51%, PAT margin 11.44%; FY27 EBITDA margin guided 17-19%.
544244|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about INR75 crore, up 20% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR12 crore (+28% YoY, 16.51% margin) and net profit of about INR8 crore (+29% YoY, 11.44% margin). Management said order booking rose about 40% YoY and first-quarter revenue is typically 20-22% of the full year. A roughly INR3 crore dispatch slipped out of the quarter due to a customer payment delay, which management said cost about 5 percentage points of growth. Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth and a 17-19% EBITDA margin range, and said FY27 working capital would stay at similar levels (around 180 days) pending a KPMG study. The call also covered a Chennai ramp-up, a planned Wada land purchase, and a reduction in forex hedging cover from 70% to 40% of export collections.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR80-85 crore same period last year

segments.name: Disc Springs (DSS)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 54% of Q1 FY27 revenue, sales +31% YoY, growth attributed mainly to the Wada plant. Disc springs are a niche category with customer buying of INR5-10 crore each.

segments.name: SFS
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of revenue, INR223 million. Management cited growing customer adoption and new business wins; the SFS cost spread versus European peers was described as 10-15% (up to 18%) on exports and 2-3% in India.

segments.name: CSS
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of revenue, INR125 million, citing steady demand across industrial and mobility applications.

segments.name: Fasteners (Chennai)
segments.commentary: New Chennai plant (4,600 MT installed capacity, high-tensile bolts) is ramping; Phase 1 utilisation about 70-80% in Q1. Wind-turbine fastener contribution is about 25-26% of Q1 sales as stated, with the offshore-wind product targeted at 10% of FY27 fastener sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 17-19%; management said it is confident and that this range holds for FY28 as well.
FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% YoY; management said it is on track or exceeding this.
Effective tax rate expected at around 20% or less, helped by deductions and a solar open-access project due for commissioning in Q3.
Working capital expected at similar levels (around 180 days) for now; KPMG study report expected by end-August 2026, with targets to be set in Q3.
Chennai Phase 1 utilisation targeted at 80-90% in Q2 and ~70% for Phase 1-2 combined by Q4; Chennai EBITDA expected to be comparable with Wada around Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
New Wada land (10-11 acre) capex of about INR40-45 crore, mostly in FY28, subject to completing the purchase (2-3 months).
capex_capacity: Chennai plant: new fastener facility with 4,600 MT installed capacity; Phase 1 utilisation ~70-80% in Q1 FY27; Phase 2 mezzanine (~10,000 sq ft) construction to finish in Q2 and more machines by Q3, required in Q4.
Chennai monthly run rate: manufacturing INR4-5 crore per month; June production ~INR4.5 crore but dispatches lower due to an item on hold.
Hot-dip galvanising (HDG) plant commissioned at Chennai, brought in-house to improve margin and delivery.
MoU signed for ~10.15 acre of land at Wada, adjacent to existing plant; ~50,000 sq ft shed planned mainly for fasteners and partly disc springs; legal due diligence underway.
Solar open-access project initiated, expected commissioning in Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Order booking up ~40% YoY, per management.
Pricing stable; management says it offers 10-20% savings to customers while holding margins, and passes through raw-material increases with a lag.
Fasteners cited as the main growth driver. Customer wallet sizes: fasteners INR50-500 crore vs disc springs INR5-10 crore.
New products (bolts, smart fasteners for offshore wind, wedge lock washers) are ~30-35% of order book, per management.
Company said it is taking share from European producers; some multi-year accounts grew share of business from 5-10% to 50-75%.
Forex: forward cover on export collections reduced from 70% to 40% due to euro volatility and war-related uncertainty; ~4% of 12-month exposure already covered.
Product mix: ~85% customised products; ~15% sold to fastener distributors at company level. Disc spring and Gallock 75-80% to OEMs; SFS >95% direct to OEMs.
Management said a single ~INR3 crore+ dispatch was held because of a customer payment delay; ex-this, growth would have been ~25%.
Management cited TAM of USD100 billion for fasteners, with Gala addressing ~USD2.5 billion including bolts and nuts.
Seatbelt retractor spring: customer approved Gala as source after July visit; small-batch supply to start, slow ramp due to safety-critical nature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin bridge from 16.51% to the 17-19% guide, across forex, Chennai leverage and mix? Also, why cut forward cover from 70% to 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY27 EBITDA margin should be 17-19% with no forex hit since exports are hedged. Jalan cited Chennai utilisation improving in Q3/Q4 and Q1 being ~20-22% of full-year revenue to absorb fixed overheads. The cut to 40% reflects euro volatility and war-related uncertainty; about 4% of 12-month exposure is covered so far.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 growth stack up, and what drove the Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Order booking up ~40% YoY. A ~INR3 crore+ dispatch was held for a customer payment delay; ex this, growth would have been ~25%. Management said it is confident of meeting or exceeding the 20-25% FY27 growth guide. DSS growth came from Wada and fastener growth from Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook, and when will KPMG study benefits show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is expected to stay at similar levels (around 180 days). The KPMG study started in July, with the report expected by end-August or in Q2; targets and actions to be set in Q3, so no firm improvement guidance yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why don't customers switch to Gala despite a 15-18% cost advantage over European peers, and how long does onboarding take?
qa_highlights.answer: Onboarding takes 12-24 months (plant approval, audit, samples, then share-of-business ramp). Some multi-year accounts grew share from 5-10% to 50-75%. Some customers with cost advantage still do not switch immediately. No customer lost on quality or delivery in 25 years.

qa_highlights.question: Seatbelt retractor spring status, land capex timing, and effective tax rate sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Customer approved Gala as source after a July visit; small-batch supply starts with a slow ramp given safety-critical use. Wada land (~10 acre MoU, 2-3 months to close) needs ~INR40-45 crore capex, mostly in FY28. ETR guided at ~20% or less, helped by 100% deductions for R&D (Sec 35(1)(i)), ESOP perquisite deduction, higher tax depreciation and a solar open-access project commissioning in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Chennai utilisation, run rate, and HDG plant impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 utilisation was ~70-80% in Q1 and is targeted at 80-90% in Q2, with Phase 1-2 combined ~70% by Q4. Chennai manufacturing runs at INR4-5 crore a month; June output was ~INR4.5 crore but dispatches were lower due to a held item. In-house HDG improved margin and delivery and unlocked some customers.

risks_watch: Customer payment delays: a ~INR3 crore+ dispatch slipped out of Q1, costing ~5 percentage points of growth; watch Q2 receivables and working capital days versus ~180 days.
Chennai ramp execution: Phase 1 utilisation must reach 80-90% in Q2 and Phase 2 machines are needed by Q4; Chennai EBITDA parity with Wada is guided only for Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trailer-axle growth of about 34% share gain, given single-digit industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely Q4 FY26 order spillover. Management declined to comment on market share; capacity expansion should allow further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst margin quarter behind us, with QoQ expansion ahead?

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-five customer revenue fall between DRHP and FY26?

544256|2026-06.headline: PNG Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to INR192.4 crore and PAT up 52% to INR105.3 crore.

EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps to 8.0% and PAT margin rose 40 bps to 4.4%, with gross margin flat at 13.2% reported. Management kept FY27 guidance (around 25 store additions to 103 stores, about 7% EBITDA margin, about INR400 crore other expenses) and flagged that Q1 other expenses were low due to cuts in marketing and no store launches. qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only about 5% despite store expansion?

544258|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.0% as Middle East crisis cut EXIM volumes 11% QoQ.
544258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA fell from INR27 crore to INR25 crore, with margin down from 5.6% to 5.0%, and PAT dropped from INR10.8 crore to INR8.3 crore. Total containers handled were 57,754, up 4.3% YoY but down 7% QoQ, with EXIM down 10.96% QoQ and domestic almost flat. For FY26, containers rose 6.14% to 2,26,578, and management attributed the shortfall from double-digit growth to the March disruption from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

Capacity on US and Europe routes is about 30-35% of normal; Cape of Good Hope diversions add about 3,500 nautical miles and 10-15 days.
Realisations were hit by geopolitical factors and are expected to improve as EXIM volumes recover.

Receivables have risen, with the company citing growth in retail MMCT customers (up 25-30% YoY) who pay only when the next consignment ships. Management said the company had INR600+ crore in receivables, a figure raised by an analyst and not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise from INR172 crore to INR217 crore despite IPO net proceeds of about INR363 crore, of which about INR163 crore went to debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects working capital needs as the new Devaliya MMCT became operational.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue, saying it operates as a consolidated multimodal logistics provider and that splitting would distort the picture.

544260|2026-03.headline: Northern Arc posted record Q4FY26 PAT of INR133 crore (up 251% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR406 crore, with AUM at INR16,594 crore (up 22% YoY).
544260|2026-03.overview: Northern Arc reported its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR133 crore in Q4FY26, taking FY26 PAT to INR406 crore (up 33% YoY). AUM grew 22% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR16,594 crore, with direct-to-customer (D2C) at 59% of AUM. Credit cost fell to 2.2% in Q4 (from 3.5% in Q3) and 2.8% for FY26, helped by the RBI's FLDG-related ECL clarification, which management said contributed a one-off benefit. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 22-25% and ROA above 3%, with ROE in the mid-to-late teens over 8-10 quarters.

rows.why: Capital adequacy fell to 24.40% (from ~29.81% in FY25 per analyst) and management is raising INR100 crore of preference capital by Sept/Oct 2026 to fund growth; no capex-to-revenue figure was given and the call framed tech spend as stable as a share of expenses.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated 35-40% AUM growth and ~3.5% ROA rather than raising them, declined quarterly profit guidance, and flagged higher borrowing costs from carrying ~INR200 crore of surplus liquidity.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 AUM grew only ~1% QoQ and the 35-40% FY27 AUM target depends on a Q2/Q3 festive jump; the ~3.5% ROA and 13-14% NIM targets are exposed to a 10.86% cost of borrowing and early-stage new product ramp-up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: MSME LAP disbursement started in Q1 FY27 (ticket INR8-20 lakh, target ~2-3% of AUM by FY27 end), e-3W battery replacement finance (~INR60,000 ticket) launched, and personal loan, top-up and used two-wheeler products are in ramp-up.

rows.label: Namma Loan (Sreesastha) South entry
rows.when: Karnataka live now; Tamil Nadu within FY27
rows.why: Karnataka disbursements have started with 100% Manba funding, FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore and breakeven expected in 9-12 months (possibly 6-7 months).

rows.label: INR100 crore preference capital raise
rows.why: Capital adequacy has fallen to 24.40% and management has a concrete plan to raise INR100 crore of preference shares by Sept/Oct 2026 to fund growth.

rows.label: Mix shift to higher-yield products
rows.why: Management targets ROA ~3.5% with ~30% of further lending in higher-IRR personal loan, top-up and used two-wheeler products, while two-wheeler share is 84.1% and is targeted to fall to 75-77% by FY27 end.

tone.note: Management was confident on 35-40% AUM growth, 3.5% ROA and the South entry, but cautious on quarterly profit and borrowing cost trajectory; analysts pushed on the capital adequacy decline (29.81% to 24.40%), the ~1% QoQ AUM growth and the rising cost of borrowing.

544262|2026-09.headline: Manba Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 20% YoY to INR14 crores, NII up 40% to INR52 crores, AUM up 21% to INR1,811 crores.
544262|2026-09.overview: Manba Finance reported Q2 FY27 net interest income of INR52 crores (up 40% YoY) and PAT of INR14 crores (up 20% YoY), with H1 NII of INR94 crores (up 39%) and H1 PAT of INR27 crores (up 28%). AUM reached INR1,811 crores at September 30, 2026, up 21% YoY, while GNPA improved to 2.96% and NNPA to 2.19%. Management said a rating upgrade to A minus stable from CARE and lower borrowing costs (average cost 10.14%) should support margins, and reiterated 30-35% AUM growth guidance for FY27 despite H1 growth of about 20%. The call was hosted by Antique Stock Broking and included mostly retail-investor questions.

segments.name: 2-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 83.10% of portfolio; main growth driver in the quarter, supported by dealer network expansion and new locations. Dealer base about 1,900-1,932 across 148 locations in 7 states.

segments.name: Top-up loans
segments.commentary: 5.70% of portfolio; secured against existing 2-wheeler customers, quoted IRR around 32%.

segments.name: 3-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 3% of portfolio. Battery replacement loan for EV 3-wheelers launched about 2 months ago, limited to own customers and to be tested for 18 months.

segments.name: Used vehicle loans
segments.commentary: 1.60% of portfolio; used 2-wheeler loans quoted at 27-28% IRR, with 100-plus dealers added in the last 6 months.

segments.name: MSME LAP / small business loans
segments.commentary: Small business loan IRR about 27-28%, average ticket INR5 lakh, NPAs 3-4%. MSME LAP disbursement at INR2-2.5 crores per month, targeted at INR5 crores per month by January.

segments.name: Personal loans
segments.commentary: Unsecured, IRR similar to top-up (around 32%); being scaled cautiously through DSAs.

guidance_outlook: AUM and disbursement growth guidance for FY27 of 30-35%; management said H1 AUM growth was about 20% and H2 festive season should close the gap.
Management expects FY28 growth to continue but gave no numerical guidance.

Borrowing costs: about INR600 crores of high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; management expects about 25 bps overall impact in Q3-Q4 and a 50-75 bps reduction in cost of funds from the rating upgrade.
NIM concern raised by an analyst: prior guidance of 13-14% versus about 12.3% currently; management said NIM would not be hit by the RBI rate hike.
Capital from INR100 crore preferential issue expected by November 6, 2026; management expects capital to support growth for 4-6 quarters.
Interim dividend of INR0.25 per share declared for FY27 (face value INR10).
capex_capacity: INR100 crore preferential issue of equity and warrants; board approved in Q2, principal approval from NSE and BSE received, funds expected by November 6, 2026.

Operations in 148 locations across 7 states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Karnataka); about 16 offices added in the last year and 5-6 more small business loan branches planned this quarter.
Karnataka launched about 60 days before the call, with 100-plus dealers onboarded; Karnataka season expected in January.
Technology spend about INR2 crores per year with a 28-person tech team; disbursement turnaround cut from 3.5-4 days to 1.5-2 days, targeted same-day by end of year.
Employee base about 2,061, of which 1,100-plus in sales; 2.45 lakh+ live customers after adding about 32,330 in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler registrations about 53 lakh units in Q2, with August and September both record highs; September retail registrations up 32% YoY per FADA.
Management expects Diwali and Navratri season to lift H2 disbursements; said October alone added INR120 crores of new AUM after run-down.
Competition in 2-wheeler loans named as IDFC, L&T and regional players such as Berar; management claims about 15% market share in locations operating for 4+ years.
Bounce rate about 18-20%, with 7-8% of customers remaining in bounce across tenure, per management.
NTC (new-to-credit) customers about 40% of the book; LTV capped at 75% for them.

qa_highlights.question: Growth timeline for newer states (UP, MP, Rajasthan) given Gujarat and Maharashtra hold about half the dealer base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Maharashtra and Gujarat dealer tie-ups are largely complete; new dealer additions are coming from Rajasthan, UP, MP and Karnataka, with 100-plus dealers onboarded in Karnataka in the first 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: How many quarters the INR100 crore raise will support growth, and FY27-28 growth guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Capital should support growth for 4-6 quarters; FY27 guidance is 30-35% growth, with H1 at about 20% and festive season in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is 30-35% AUM growth achievable given H1 AUM growth of about INR98 crores, and any El Nino impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said October added INR120 crores of AUM and similar is expected in November; MSME LAP and small business loans, 5-6 new branches and 10-12 live BC partners were cited as additional drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Operating expenses up 28% YoY in Q2; drivers and cost optimisation.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to 16 new offices in the last year, Karnataka expansion and seasonal sales hiring, and said YoY cost comparison is not a fair measure given the expansion; NIM, average cost and credit cost were said to be improving QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Further cost-of-funds reduction and NIM trajectory (guidance 13-14% vs 12.3% currently).
qa_highlights.answer: About INR600 crores of old high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; overall impact of about 25 bps expected in Q3-Q4, and new borrowings are at lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Share of NTC borrowers and delinquency comparison; used vehicle and high-yield products.
qa_highlights.answer: NTC share about 40%; behaviour broadly similar to other customers except those with CIBIL above 750. Used 2-wheeler IRR 27-28%, top-up and personal loan IRR about 32%.

risks_watch: AUM growth of 30-35% requires roughly INR400-450 crores of H2 additions versus H1 growth of about 20%; festive-season delivery is key.
Rising RBI repo rate versus management's expectation of 50-75 bps cost-of-funds reduction from the rating upgrade.
NIM at about 12.3% versus prior 13-14% guidance.
Operating expense growth of 28% YoY in Q2 with ongoing branch expansion.
Concentration in 2-wheeler (83.10%) and unsecured personal loans being scaled up; EV battery replacement product is untested.
Completion of the INR100 crore preferential issue by November 6, 2026.
544262|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and funding costs, with management repeatedly citing festive-season momentum and the rating upgrade. Cautious on personal loans and the EV battery product, which are being tested slowly. Somewhat evasive on the NIM gap versus guidance and on the cost-growth question, which it deflected to expansion and QoQ trends.
key_quotes: So, comfortably we will reach our 30% to 35% of growth '27.
Overall, it will help to increase my overall yield also.
So, onboarding defaulted customer is zero.

vs INR398 crores in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.change: Declined; management cited 72 bps reduction post upgrade

rows.why: Management expects about 25 bps overall cost-of-funds benefit in Q3-Q4 and a 50-75 bps reduction from the CARE upgrade to A minus, but NIM is about 12.3% versus prior 13-14% guidance, so the gap is unresolved.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 16 offices were added in the last year to reach 148 locations, with 5-6 more small business loan branches planned this quarter and Karnataka launched about 60 days before the call with 100-plus dealers onboarded.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 AUM growth was about 20% against 30-35% FY27 guidance, so H2 needs roughly INR400-450 crores of additions; October alone added INR120 crores and Q2 disbursements rose to INR267 crores from INR233 crores.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed and the INR100 crore preferential issue is funding growth for 4-6 quarters, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 AUM guidance of 30-35% was reiterated against H1 growth of about 20%, so the call does not point to a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 AUM growth of about 20% leaves a 30-35% FY27 target dependent on festive-season H2 additions, and the Q2 opex rise of 28% YoY and rising RBI repo rate are headwinds.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: EV 3-wheeler battery replacement loan launched about 2 months ago is limited to own customers and will be tested for 18 months; personal loans are being scaled cautiously through DSAs.

rows.label: High-cost borrowing repayment by March 2027
rows.why: About INR600 crores of high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027, with about 25 bps overall impact expected in Q3-Q4 FY27 and average cost of borrowing at 10.14%.

rows.label: INR100 crore preferential issue
rows.why: Board approved in Q2 with NSE and BSE principal approval received; capital adequacy is 24.69% before the issue and management expects it to support growth for 4-6 quarters.

rows.label: Karnataka season and dealer expansion in Rajasthan, UP, MP
rows.why: Karnataka has 100-plus dealers onboarded in 60 days with its season expected in January, and new dealer additions are coming from Rajasthan, UP, MP and Karnataka while Maharashtra and Gujarat tie-ups are largely complete.

tone.note: Management was confident on festive-season growth, funding cost reduction and the rating upgrade, but cautious on personal loans and the EV battery product, and evasive on the NIM gap versus 13-14% guidance and on the 28% YoY opex rise; analysts pressed on the H2 AUM bridge and NIM.

544263|2026-03.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
544263|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
Solar plant installed and operational.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables build-up; inventory normalisation timeline (about six months) and the Rs.500 crore equity raise, whose use is unconfirmed.
BIS certification issue on inner groove tube (deadline around 20-28 May 2026) could drive imports and inventory build-up.
Copper and aluminium price volatility in recent weeks, which management said is beyond expectation; pass-through has a one-quarter lag.
Geopolitical disruption to UAE dispatches and freight costs.
Ramp-up pace of the new facility versus 50%/80% utilisation targets; Q4 incremental revenue from the new facility was about Rs.15-16 crore per an analyst's estimate.
Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.
544263|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, data centre demand and utilisation targets, but evasive on the Rs.500 crore fund raise, the Rs.120 crore UAE order, the Q4 non-fin-and-tube share and the specific data centre order book. Several answers were vague or deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: Yes, even I can say next eight quarters will be highest ever. So, this quarter also will be average but number I cannot disclose.
So, now we have eight new businesses, so that is also we have to build the inventory.
Of course, slight improvement will be there, but honestly in the last two, three weeks in this copper and aluminum silver price is beyond the expectation because they sharply increase.

rows.why: New HVAC facility inaugurated 11 March 2026 and fully shifted the week before the call, with HVAC utilisation at about 15% in FY26 and targets of 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28, so the capacity is already live but still ramping.

rows.why: Fin and tube growth is guided above 80-90% (mainly data centres, about 16-19% of revenue), HVAC utilisation targets 50% in FY27 from 15% in FY26, and the old facility is fully utilised, with Vertiv approval and a Rs.120 crore export order book supporting it.

rows.why: Further capex on the existing facility is only Rs.30-40 crore over two years for line balancing, and the Rs.500 crore board-approved enabling fund raise has no finalised objective, so a larger capex announcement is conditional on the raise and not firmly guided.

rows.why: Management expects the next eight quarters to be the highest ever and export to roughly double from about Rs.100 crore on a Rs.120 crore export order book, but no revenue figure was guided and the analyst's Rs.2,250-2,850 crore target was not confirmed.

rows.why: Inventory is about 3x YoY and receivables up 1-2x, with normalisation taking about six months, and copper/aluminium volatility passes through with a one-quarter lag, so working capital and margin timing could disappoint even though no cut was guided.

rows.when: Q3 FY27 (micro-channel by end 2026 or early 2027)
rows.why: Micro-channel (MCHX) product is guided for end 2026 or early 2027 and about eight new products were already added, with bus AC, bar and plate and frost-free evaporators in supply.

rows.why: Bus AC revenue was only about Rs.10 crore in FY26 and two to three OEMs are onboarded, but no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified, so the target rests on unconfirmed orders.

rows.why: Inventory days are about 2.5 months and management expects normalisation in about six months, with about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material and Rs.8 crore of unbilled export stock as drivers.

rows.why: The board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore because IPO proceeds were exceeded by facility investment, but the objective is not finalised and bank funding is an alternative.

544264|2026-03.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.
544264|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,415.74 million (+38.08% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income was INR206.89 million (+39.96%), at a 14.61% margin. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR4,066.28 million (+21.28%) with PAT of INR504.1 million (+39.87%). Standalone growth was weaker: Q4 revenue +12.18% and Q4 PAT down 3.05%, which management attributed to capacity constraints in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering running at about 85-90% utilisation. Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations Q4 FY26
Consolidated EBITDA excl. other income Q4 FY26
Consolidated EBITDA excl. other income FY26
Standalone EBITDA excl. other income Q4 FY26
Standalone EBITDA excl. other income FY26

segments.name: Welding consumables (products)
segments.commentary: Management cited roughly 30% of revenue; under 3% (said 2-3%) of the business is conventional, with the rest special hard-facing and repair electrodes. Wires line at 85-90% utilisation; new wire line expected July 2026.

segments.name: Wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Cited at roughly 30% of revenue combined with heavy engineering; running at 85-90% utilisation, and expected to grow faster than consumables. Roller-press rolls, steel mill rollers and VRM rollers are cited as growth areas; first VRM order won.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.name: Railways (developmental)
segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.name: Defence (Tejorup Sunmay Systems)
segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 20%, supported by capacity additions, order inflows and higher-margin engineered products.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 80-100 basis points, aided by operating leverage and cost consolidation; gross margin may come under pressure from raw material volatility.
Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

Capex of about INR100 crores from IPO proceeds (INR70 crores for wear part/plate/heavy engineering, INR30 crores for electrode and slitting facility) is expected to support INR800-900 crores revenue; no additional capex planned for INR650 crores.
Debtor days targeted at 80-85 for FY27 and inventory days at 60-65; FY26 debtor days were 98 and inventory days 66.
International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.
Current utilisation: wires about 85-90%; wear plates and heavy engineering about 85-90%. Management expects utilisation to fall to roughly 50-60% once new shop floors are live.
New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

EBITDA margin eased to 12.85% from 13.12%, which management attributed to higher raw material and employee costs as a share of sales. Standalone PAT fell YoY to INR99.79 million, but this reflects a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend in the year-ago quarter. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.name: Defence

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Management said domestic drove most of Q1 growth because Q1 FY26 had large export orders; Turkey has turned out of loss, and UAE facility is expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 20% growth in FY27 and FY28 and continuing for 3-4 years, with an aim to double revenue in about three years.
EBITDA margin expected to rise 100-200 basis points over FY27 and FY28; management said Q1 margin should return to prior-year Q1 levels.

544277|2026-03.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
544277|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.
Cell utilisation assumed 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW capacity; 28 GW modules, 4 GW inverters, 20,000 MVA transformers and 1 GW electrolyser to run at full throttle in FY28.
Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating EBITDA margin fall sharply QoQ, and what are the DCR and non-DCR realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export mix low in Q4 and what is the order book composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ingot-wafer capex rise and its timeline move to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS unit economics and FY29 revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS margin guided at 18-20% without policy support. Management declined to give FY29 revenue guidance, pointing to the 20 GWh capacity and $110-120/MWh pricing.

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
544277|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

544280|2026-03.headline: Afcons posted its first-ever quarterly loss (Q4 net loss INR 89 crore) and FY26 PAT fell to INR 251 crore; no FY27 revenue or margin guidance given.
544280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 18% YoY to INR 2,777 crore and EBITDA dropped to INR 170 crore from INR 415 crore, with a net loss of INR 89 crore. Management blamed customer payment delays, overseas supply-chain disruption from the Middle East conflict, one-off provisions and marine cost overruns, and failure to cross margin-recognition thresholds on some projects. FY26 revenue was INR 12,322 crore (down 5.4%), EBITDA INR 1,439 crore (11.7% margin) and PAT INR 251 crore after a INR 76 crore Labour Code charge. Management guided FY26 order booking of INR 30,000 crore for FY27 but declined to give revenue or margin guidance until visibility improves.

segments.name: Overseas projects
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 turnover came from overseas, though overseas is only about 13% of the current order book; Q4 execution there was hit by fuel, gas and logistics disruption linked to the Middle East war, with materials routed via Dubai.

segments.name: Domestic projects
segments.commentary: Management estimated about 25% of domestic projects were affected in March; UP Jal Jeevan Mission payments are being withheld until 100% completion, against a contractual stage-wise payment basis.

segments.name: Other income
segments.commentary: FY26 other income of INR 374 crore is treated as operating income; of this, arbitration interest was INR 19 crore and other interest INR 61 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crore; about INR 15,000 crore is described as near-certain including L1 positions, with the balance to be won.
No revenue growth or EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 or Q1 FY27, citing geopolitical uncertainty, elongated award cycles and payment issues.
FY27 capex guided at about INR 725 crore; FY26 capex was INR 1,069 crore.
Management expects a sizable drop in debt in FY27, but warned that Q1 and Q2 debt typically rise.
Expects about INR 1,000 crore of stuck receivables to be liquidated by June 2026; working capital days (currently about 143) targeted at about 120 days, with no firm commitment beyond that.
Expects tunnelling to begin on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 package before the end of the next quarter, after the second TBM reached site.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 1,069 crore, of which about INR 700 crore was in Q4; FY27 capex guided at about INR 725 crore.

FY26 depreciation included INR 454 crore accelerated depreciation on TBMs; normal depreciation about INR 289 crore; Q4 depreciation about INR 100 crore per quarter, expected to rise modestly in FY27 as TBM additions of about INR 1,000 crore hit gross block.
Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 tunnel boring machine second consignment received; tunnelling expected to start before end of next quarter, and the package may extend by 12-15 months.
HRRL crude oil terminal at Mundra commissioned in FY26; Bangalore double-decker metro and Delhi-Meerut RRTS sections operational.
demand_pricing: FY26 order inflow was INR 4,125 crore excluding about INR 3,800 crore of variation and change orders; intake was below plan due to deferred awards and slow L1 conversion.
Order book about INR 31,000-32,500 crore; about 80% government, split roughly 50% state and 50% central; states include Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, MP, Rajasthan, UP and Bihar.

Since 31 March: about INR 8,000 crore of orders secured, including Croatia railway (about INR 7,544 crore) and DMRC underground metro (INR 373 crore); L1 positions of about INR 7,000 crore including Vadhavan (about INR 5,300 crore).

Two Croatia road tenders where Afcons was L1 were cancelled by the client on budget grounds; Pune Ring Road and Nagpur-Gondiya L1 positions were removed after rebid instructions, with Pune Ring Road possibly re-tendered around June.
Bid pipeline about INR 4 lakh crore over two years (70% domestic, 30% overseas); FY27 INR 30,000 crore mix stated as about 60% domestic and 40% international.

Domestic contracts carry escalation formulas (steel, cement, labour, fuel); overseas contracts mostly fixed-price with internal contingency. Croatia contract absorbs up to 10% cost increase, with pass-through above that.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 so far below the mid-quarter confidence expressed on the Q3 call, and what drove the miss?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 customer payments did not come as in the past 15-20 years; Afcons chose liquidity over growth, funding projects only up to limits, and overseas supply disruption in March (fuel, gas, logistics) hit execution.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Total one-offs of about INR 260-265 crore: about INR 160 crore of Q4 provisions (including an ECL matrix shift), a significant arbitration-related provision, and extra cost on a marine project. Management said no further provisions were made in Q1 FY27 to date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of finance cost and the rise in interest?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of customer advances in FY26 were interest-bearing versus a partial-year effect in FY25; average borrowing rose and rate cuts did not fully offset the increase.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book and receivables are affected by payment delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Payment delays are widespread; apart from UP Jal Jeevan Mission and a Gabon project, no specific names were disclosed. Projects below 10% completion carry about two months of receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance when order book is about INR 60,000 crore after inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited long gestation projects (four dams of about five years; HSR package extended 12-15 months), elongated award cycles, and fuel and geopolitical uncertainty, saying revenue visibility is not yet adequate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Gabon bank guarantee impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Gabon bank guarantee invoked and paid; the contract was already loss-provided with no margin recognised, and about 92% complete.

risks_watch: Receivable collections: about INR 1,000 crore unlock expected by June; working capital days at about 143 versus 120-day target.
Interest-bearing customer advances (about 40% of advances) keep finance cost elevated while margins are not yet recognised on several projects.
Overseas execution (about 30% of turnover) exposed to fuel, gas and logistics disruption; fixed-price contracts with limited pass-through.
Order conversion: about INR 7,000 crore of L1 positions still to convert; Pune Ring Road and Nagpur-Gondiya rebidding; further Croatia-type cancellations possible.
Govt. payment delays (UP Jal Jeevan Mission, state treasury) and labour availability/cost under the new Labour Code.
Debt trajectory: management expects a sizable FY27 debt reduction, but Q1-Q2 debt typically rises.
544280|2026-03.management_tone: Defensive and apologetic at the outset, with the MD saying he is personally upset; the CFO's answers were detailed on one-offs but evasive on forward payments and margins, repeatedly declining guidance pending visibility.
key_quotes: I apologize to all the investors that we have made a loss in the quarter for the first time since we started publishing quarterly numbers from 2010.

Having a certainty of about INR 15,000 crores order including L1 in the current financial year, we expect to book another INR 15,000 crores of more orders, making a total order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crores for the current financial year.

At this stage, considering the continued uncertainty in the geopolitical environment, elongated award cycles and ongoing project-related developments, we believe it would be prudent to wait for greater visibility before providing specific revenue growth or EBITDA margin guidance for FY27.

544280|2026-06.headline: Afcons Q1 FY27 revenue fell 20% to INR2,727 crore and PAT to INR30 crore; management expects H2-weighted recovery with no formal guidance.
544280|2026-06.overview: Total income fell 20.3% YoY to INR2,727 crore (incl. INR56 crore other income) and EBITDA dropped 41% to INR263 crore at a 9.6% margin, while PAT fell to INR30 crore from INR137 crore. Management attributed the weakness to weather, slow land handover, labour shortages, pending clearances, stretched client payments (notably UP Jal Jeevan Mission) and lower turnover that left overheads uncovered. Order inflow was strong at INR13,219 crore, lifting order book to INR43,290 crore, while working capital and debt rose. Management declined to give revenue or profit guidance, pointing to Q3 and Q4 for a pickup.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said symptoms are visible; Maharashtra government is resolving land issues, and an MP compensation issue is near resolution. Q3 and Q4 are expected to show a significant uptick.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for Croatia, Vadhvan and HSR and HSR payments?
qa_highlights.answer: Croatia sees minimal spend in FY27 and picks up in FY28; Vadhvan is limited to geotechnical and design work this year. HSR past billing has been paid regularly and tunnelling turnover begins from November.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue and H2 growth trajectory?

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt, working capital days and balance sheet numbers?

qa_highlights.question: Asset-light model versus owning equipment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it invests only in strategic equipment; overseas rentals are costly, equipment is paid back in about 9 months in Africa versus 48-60 months in India, and marine fleet is strategic.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow upside beyond INR30,000 crore?

Sequentially, reported revenue fell because about $24.8 million of Q4 open-enrolment revenue did not recur, but steady-state organic revenue grew 5.1% QoQ in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.9% to INR 4,716 million at a 24.0% margin (down from 24.9% in Q4), and adjusted PAT rose 35.1% to INR 2,697 million at 13.7%. Management reiterated low double-digit FY27 organic constant-currency growth and the 24-25% margin range, with the wage impact absorbed via efficiencies and FX.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the low double-digit guidance not higher given 5% QoQ underlying growth?

544282|2026-09.headline: Sagility Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% YoY in INR to INR 20,321 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin hit 26.3%, and FY27 margin guidance was raised to 25-26%.
544282|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 20,321 mn ($212.6 mn), up 22.5% YoY in INR and 12.2% in constant currency, with organic growth of 11.9% in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to INR 5,353 mn at a 26.3% margin, the highest in six quarters, helped by operating efficiencies, FX tailwinds and geo mix despite higher statutory wage costs. Management acquired Chirok Health LLC (closed October 21, 2026) to build a mid-cycle RCM capability and push provider growth, and raised FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 25-26% from 24-25%. The company now holds a net cash position of INR 1,127 mn, and management expects open enrolment/AEP revenue to be slightly lower than last year.

+23% YoY; margin up from 24% in Q1

segments.commentary: Accounted for 89.9% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Management said the mix is shifting toward managed services and AI-led deals, and that a Big Ten health plan win covers over 10 mn members with minimum potential ACV above $10 mn.

segments.name: Providers
segments.commentary: Accounted for 10.1% of Q2 revenue and has grown at about 10-11%, lagging payers. Revenue tapered from some discrete projects with one provider client; Chirok acquisition is intended to accelerate this segment.
