segments.commentary: Clinical documentation improvement, medical coding, risk adjustment, HEDIS/quality. TTM revenue to Sep 2026 of $13 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin 35.8%, net revenue retention above 115%, 750+ employees mostly in India. Consideration $20 mn upfront plus up to $12.35 mn earn-out tied to CY27-CY28 revenue targets.

segments.name: CareSeed (acquired last quarter)
segments.commentary: Integrated into clinical practice; strengthens Medicare Advantage quality capability and adds mid- and small-sized clients. Contributed to the gap between reported 22.5% and organic 22.2% growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of low double digits in constant currency maintained; Chirok and CareSeed revenue sits on top of organic guidance.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 25-26% from 24-25%; management said it sees 24-26% as the structural range, with possible marginal upside if AI productivity gains are retained.

OE/AEP revenue expected to be slightly lower than last year, roughly 100 bps lower as a share of total revenue (last year about 6%); marginally below flat YoY per CFO; subject to change over coming weeks.
Management intends to repay all outstanding debt in full during FY27.
Interim dividend of INR 0.15 per share approved, payable in Q3 FY27.
No explicit provider revenue-share target given; management declined to give Chirok guidance until late FY27.

Employee strength 51,486 at end Q2; quarterly voluntary attrition 25.7%, down from 28.6% in Q1 FY27 and lower than Q2 FY26.
Delivery centre count fell to 28 from 31 in March 2026 (33 in FY25), but management said this reflects counting multiple facilities on one campus as one site; seat count continued to rise.
Some short-term leases used during site consolidation; Jamaica sites closed earlier.
Staffing to capacity for AEP season with some flex capacity available.
105 active client groups; all top 10 client groups above $20 mn TTM revenue for the first time.
demand_pricing: Deal ACV up 18.2% YoY to $40.2 mn in Q2, from wins across 31 existing clients and one new client.
Payment integrity win from a Big Ten health plan is contingency-based, so revenue builds over time.
Clients making more deliberate, senior-level buying decisions for large transformation deals; pipeline skewed to managed services and mid-market Blues plans.
Agentic AI deployments: Synchrony Claims Lifecycle (claims adjudication) and Synchrony RCM Lifecycle (denials and appeals), with humans in the loop.
Management said provider deals have historically been smaller; gross margin difference between payer and provider is about 200-300 bps and deal-specific.
On AI pricing, most productivity gains will be passed to clients, with some retained.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin improvement and what supports the raised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited operating efficiencies, a small FX tailwind from Q1 to Q2, and favourable geo mix; he expects FX to stay broadly at current levels and efficiencies to continue for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much could open enrolment contribution fall this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said about 100 bps lower than last year's roughly 6% of revenue on current visibility; CFO said it is marginally below flat YoY at this early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Is Chirok a step-up in provider mix, and is there an explicit provider target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is a much larger provider share over time but gave no explicit 2-3 year target; provider share is about 10% today. Investment is mainly the Chirok deal plus a dedicated provider go-to-market team, with no major margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is provider growth lagging, and what is Chirok's growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Provider growth has been 10-11% with some revenue taper from discrete projects at one client. Chirok revenue dipped in 2023-24 when one client's volumes fell, then recovered; management said the 35.8% margin is broadly on the same basis as Sagility's adjusted EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is there conflict in serving both payers and providers?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said there is no inherent conflict, citing about 15 years of running both businesses and claims-denial friction the company helps resolve.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin stay in 24-26% range or structurally rise with AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said the range remains 24-26%, with possible gradual upside if the company keeps some AI productivity benefits; most gains are expected to flow to clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the minimum wage impacts and delivery centre trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the full minimum wage impact is baked into guidance (Q2 about INR 148 mn vs INR 70 mn in Q1), with Karnataka and Telangana effective end May and 1 June. The drop in site count reflects campus consolidation.

risks_watch: OE/AEP revenue is running slightly below last year, and the number could still shift over the coming weeks.
Chirok revenue per headcount is well below a listed Indian provider peer; management could not explain the gap and will follow up. Chirok pricing is said to be at market.
Chirok's AI disruption exposure in mid-cycle RCM: management says outpatient coding is most vulnerable, while inpatient coding is less exposed.
Provider growth has lagged payers; watch whether Chirok and cross-selling lift provider growth above 10-11%.
Statutory minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana are a continuing cost headwind; any stay would be upside.
Q2 margin benefited from FX and geo mix, so sustainability depends on FX staying near current levels.
Earn-out payments on Chirok (up to $12.35 mn) and the $10 mn+ payment integrity deal depend on revenue milestones, so timing is uncertain.
Possible acquisitions: management said it stays open to clinical capability or client-focused tuck-ins, but named no specific target.
544282|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operations and margins, with management raising margin guidance and citing record-level Q2 profitability. More cautious on AEP/OE season, which is described as early and subject to change, and evasive on some detail: Chirok revenue per head, the ACV split between payers and providers, and an explicit provider target were all deferred.
key_quotes: We are pleased with the progress that we have made through the first half of FY '27. The business momentum has been strong.
Operating profitability remains strong with Q2 adjusted EBITDA at INR 5,353 million, or $56 million, representing a year -on-year growth of 23%, with a margin of 26.3%, the highest in six quarters.
But over a period of time, it could marginally increase if we manage to retain the benefits of AI.
Like I said, it's exactly to accelerate the growth in the provider segment.
So this is not an acquisition where we want to try and improve the margins of Chirok.

rows.why: Chirok closed with $20 mn upfront plus up to $12.35 mn earn-out on TTM revenue of $13 mn at a 35.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, adding a provider-side RCM capability on top of organic guidance.

544283|2026-03.headline: ACME Solar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR705 crore, FY26 revenue INR2,507 crore (+59%), with 2.3 GW of merchant BESS now running.
544283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR705 crore (+31% YoY), including INR157 crore of other income, and FY26 revenue was INR2,507 crore (+59%) on capacity addition and higher CUF. PAT was INR138 crore for the quarter (19.6% margin) and INR498 crore for FY26 (19.9%), with management citing EBITDA margins above 90%. Management said about 2.3 GW of BESS is now commissioned and earning on merchant and short-term contracts at roughly INR2.2 crore per day. Management also flagged a timeline shift: most of the 1.5 GW generation commissioning and the 10 GWh BESS target depend on CTU substations, some of which are delayed by up to about 6 months.

Weighted average cost of debt (operational projects)
financial_highlights.change: Refinancing cut rate by ~150 bps on INR3,300 crore

segments.name: Solar and wind generation (operational)
segments.commentary: Operational contracted generation capacity is 2,990 MW. Management said plant and grid availability were above 99% for the year, and FY26 portfolio CUF was about 26%. Sikar (Rajasthan) new plants ran at about 29-30% CUF for the year, and roughly 28%+ in Q4.

segments.name: BESS (merchant)
segments.commentary: About 2.3 GWh of BESS is commissioned, mostly in March, and earns about INR2.2 crore per day net (over INR60 crore per month) from tariff arbitrage. Round-trip efficiency is 88-90%. Management said the Q3 battery contribution was negligible.

guidance_outlook: Target of about 1.5 GW of generation projects commissioned in FY27, with the first FDRE commissioning at Neemuch substation in June 2026.

Battery target of about 10 GWh for the next calendar year: roughly 8.5 GWh merchant and 1.5 GWh in FDRE format. Management said the 10 GWh target is achievable on connectivity and financing; supply and geopolitics are the main uncertainties.
Around 2.5 GW of connectivity at operational substations (Fatehgarh-1, Fatehgarh-2 under STOA, Bikaner-3) is ready for BESS discharge at night.
Under-construction portfolio of 5.1 GW (total pipeline 8,071 MW) with PPA-signed capacity of 3,280 MW; PPA-signed projects expected to be commissioned by FY28.
Management expects a run-rate EBITDA jump as battery revenue starts; a 75-80% EBITDA margin is expected on merchant BESS at INR6 tariff arbitrage.
capex_capacity: Committed total capex INR12,475 crore: INR6,445 crore incurred in FY26 and INR6,030 crore in purchase orders. Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in Q4.
Gross block rose about INR3,460 crore in FY26, of which about INR1,000-1,100 crore is battery.

Capital advances of about INR323 crore, mainly battery (10% advance against bank guarantee) and turbines (20% advance). Management said solar module capex is being deferred until the LTA is operational.
Under-construction portfolio added 301 MW of peak-power FDRE with SECI in the quarter; total under construction is 5.1 GW, requiring about 17 GWh of BESS.

Commissioning timeline: NTPC hybrid solar ready, LTA by December 2026; Pachora wind component a couple of quarters later; SJVN Fatehgarh full FDRE by FY27 end (LTA March 2027). Pavagada and Anantapur are targeted this year per CTU timelines.
demand_pricing: India peak demand hit 256 GW on 25 April 2026, against 250 GW in May 2024. Electricity consumption grew 8.9% in April 2026.

India added about 55 GW of RE in FY26 (cumulative 283 GW). Management expects peak-power and FDRE/BESS-linked bids to dominate, with 15-20 GW of bids this year (fewer than last year) and state plus central tenders of 20-30 GW.

Management said peak-power products sell fastest, followed by partial peak, then wind; plain solar sells slowest. Thermal-equivalent BESS pricing is cited at INR9-10 per unit at peak, with the annual realisation at INR7-8.
Receivable days have fallen to about 14-15 days from about 180 days in the past. Trade receivables fell 13% YoY. Central offtakers take a cash discount and pay in about 10 days.

qa_highlights.question: What battery capex was incurred and how much BESS capacity was commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in the last quarter, and about 1.3 GWh was commissioned as of the prior quarter. Battery capacity reached 2.3 GWh by the time of the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate EBITDA from existing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EBITDA including other income was about INR2,200 crore, mainly from the PPA projects. BESS revenue at INR2.2 crore per day is over INR60 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is there curtailment, and how is future project allocation shaped?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 2 projects are connected to the state grid. FY26 curtailment impact was INR5-6 crore, plus INR3 crore of STU impact in Rajasthan. Nearly all of the portfolio is on CTU, with the goal that each project has a battery.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross block growing faster than run-rate EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,000-1,100 crore of the gross block increase is battery, and the battery was commissioned late in the year, so it is not yet in run-rate EBITDA. Wind is also still ramping in phases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from LOA conversion and CERC connectivity rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 6.2 GW of signed PPAs are under construction, and 3.2 GW of LOA has converted to PPA. Management does not expect LOAs to be surrendered, and it has a backup plan of using connectivity for future bids or battery-linked projects.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the BESS arbitrage last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duration is uncertain. It estimated the national need at about 200-300 GWh, and said the peak price should stay at INR7-8 for four to five years given gas constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Are CTU substation delays affecting commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 60% of substations are on time and the maximum delay is typically 6 months. Where delays are known, modules are deferred, and no penalty applies under the sync-up framework.

risks_watch: Commissioning timelines depend on CTU substations and LTA dates; management cites delays of up to about 6 months, with the 1.5 GW FY27 target at risk.
BESS merchant revenue depends on the peak-offpeak price spread; management concedes the duration is uncertain and the spread could narrow as more batteries come online.
The 10 GWh battery target depends on supply of material and geopolitical factors.
CERC draft proposal on LOA-based connectivity and PPA signing risk for about 850 MW of older PPAs still in discussion.
Q4 PLF fell about 1% YoY, which management attributed to lower irradiation and curtailment.
Management commentary on the new CFO is that Arun Chopra has replaced Rajat Kumar Singh; watch for continuity.

So technically, maybe 25 to 30 gigawatt will technically mean solar of 40, 50 gigawatt.

544283|2026-06.headline: ACME Solar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to INR954 crore and EBITDA 56% to INR831 crore, with BESS contributing INR226 crore.
544283|2026-06.overview: Management reported record revenue and EBITDA for Q1 FY27, with total revenue of INR954 crore (up 63% YoY), EBITDA of INR831 crore (up 56%) and PAT of INR235 crore (up 80%). Growth was attributed to a record CUF of 30.9%, BESS revenue and new renewable capacity. BESS commissioning reached about 3.62 GWh cumulative, and the BESS commissioning guidance was pulled forward to more than 10 GWh by FY27 from calendar 2027. Management also said it has locked in about INR1,400 crore of short-term BESS revenue for FY27 and addressed a fire at the ACME Suryodaya BESS site, attributing it to an AC cabling short circuit rather than the battery system.

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to charging power cost in opex

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar/FDRE)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin ~88-89% in Q1; ex-BESS EBITDA margin stated at ~91%, with seasonal range of 88-91% over recent quarters. Management cited repowering of existing plants as a margin support.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR226 crore in Q1 with ~82% EBITDA margin; cumulative commissioned capacity ~3.62 GWh (about 40% of India's cumulative commissioned BESS). Management cites an annual EBITDA-to-capex yield above 20%.

guidance_outlook: BESS commissioning target raised to more than 10 GWh by FY27 (earlier: 10 GWh by calendar 2027), roughly three quarters earlier.
Around 1.5 GW of contracted renewable capacity to be commissioned in FY27, subject to substation and transmission availability.
Full-year FY27 capex upgraded to approximately INR15,000-20,000 crore.
About INR1,400 crore of BESS revenue locked for FY27 on roughly 70-80% of the ~10 GWh target; management said it could be higher if more volume is contracted.
Management indicated a 2-3 year assumption of INR1,400 crore-plus BESS revenue is reasonable; BESS EBITDA margin expected within 2-5% of Q1 level (~82%).
Management said it may increase its 2030 target beyond 10 GWh, to be updated in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 8,070 MW, with about 20 GWh of battery storage; under-construction capacity 5,080 MW.
PPAs signed for 3,880 MW, including 600 MW of new FDRE and hybrid PPAs with SECI this quarter; about 1,200 MW still awaiting PPA signing.
Debt tied up for about 85% of PPA-signed portfolio; INR6,000 crore financing secured for 700 MW of under-construction FDRE projects.
Battery procurement: more than 15 GWh ordered (CATL, Hithium); around 90% of the 20 GWh battery requirement contracted, with orders placed where PPAs are signed.

BESS capex ~INR93 lakh per MW including transformer, IDC and EPC; management said it could rise 5-10% for future batches. More than $300 million hedged at roughly $89-93 per unit of USD exchange rate.
Battery operations: round-trip efficiency ~89%, depth of discharge ~93%, state of health above 99.9%, availability above 99%; operating at one cycle per day.
demand_pricing: India power demand grew 8.8% YoY in Q1 to 485 billion units; peak demand hit a record 271 GW and was near 270 GW in July.
Short-term BESS realisations cited at INR8-10/kWh (publicly available DEEP portal and HP-TAM bids), sometimes higher; contracts are typically under one year, with 6-9 months' lead time.
Open (merchant) BESS capacity is about 600 MWh; management aims for zero open capacity outside PPA by end-2026, though a 300 MW plant is still open.

SECI is consolidating bids and will only bid with firmer power-offtake commitments, reducing near-term bid volumes; management expects large FDRE, peak power, CFD and state bids to follow over 6-9 months.
Management sees the peak-power market growing toward 300-500 GWh, potentially 1 TWh in a positive case, driven by rooftop and KUSUM solar (duck-curve effect).
Competition from other BESS entrants (including Adani) is rising, but management argues merchant supply will remain limited and that the market is still new to state buyers.

qa_highlights.question: How much open or early BESS capacity will there be in FY27 and the next couple of years, and what are realisations on the INR1,400 crore short-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is contracting well above 10 GWh and realisations are INR8-10 per unit, depending on month and volume. Only ~600 MWh is open today, with a target of zero open capacity outside PPAs by end-2026. Management plans for 10-12 GWh to remain available for short-term markets each year over the next five years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the curtailment impact and what drove EBITDA growth ex-BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment was about 1% of revenue, only on state-based projects. EBITDA growth was attributed to CUF (30.9% vs 28.5%) and repowering of existing plants. Management is considering adding batteries to state projects to absorb surplus generation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,400 crore revenue sustainable for 2-3 years, given El Nino-driven pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the 10 GWh base supporting INR1,400 crore-plus for the next 2-3 years based on PPA and GNA timelines. Beyond that, it depends on market pricing and new PPAs. It said the market is still untapped by most discoms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core (ex-BESS) EBITDA margin and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-BESS margin was ~91% in Q1, with a seasonal range of 88-91%. Management expects FDRE projects may lift margins because their realisations are healthier than plain solar.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 6.28 INR/kWh PPA and the hybrid configuration changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The hybrid project was offered with 1 hour of battery, a change from the standard configuration. The other project at INR6.28 per unit has no change in configuration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for C&I and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has started hiring for data-centre opportunities but is focused on profitability. It intends to target CTU-connected C&I customers and will not dilute mid-to-high teen return targets.

risks_watch: Execution on BESS commissioning: cumulative ~3.62 GWh must reach more than 10 GWh by FY27, with about 20% of that capacity still uncontracted and dependent on supply chain and timing.

Revenue sustainability beyond 2-3 years: the INR1,400 crore short-term BESS book depends on El Nino-driven state demand, realisations of INR8-10 per unit, and new PPAs or bids as SECI bid volumes have fallen.

Grid and transmission dependence: 1.5 GW FY27 renewable commissioning is tied to substation and GNA availability (SJVN FDRE GNA around June 2027), with curtailment about 1% of revenue on state projects.
Rising BESS competition (Adani and other entrants) and possible pricing compression on merchant spreads; about 600 MWh still open with a 300 MW plant unallocated.
Capex and cost risk: FY27 capex raised to INR15,000-20,000 crore; BESS cost could rise 5-10% for future batches, with about $300 million hedged at roughly $89-93 per unit of USD exchange rate.

Cautious or non-committal on post-FY27 pricing and volumes (management said it would confirm when deliveries are made), and on the timing of solar GNA and the fire root cause, which it described as already resolved.
